John laughed as he swung higher and higher on the swings. He waved his arms in the air and shouted out loud. When the swing came to a stop, he jumped off and ran to the slide.

John loved to slide down. His dad held his arms as he went up the ladder, and then once he was at the top, he said "1,2,3" and John slid down. He shouted out with joy as he went faster and faster.

When the day was over, John and his parents went home. He felt so happy and nice that he had gotten to do all these fun things. John would never forget his special day at the park!

Once there was a black cat. He was very quiet and deaf. His name was Tom. Everyday he would go out and explore. Tom loved to explore!

One day he went for a walk, and he followed an old man down the street. The old man had a long black hat, a big grey coat, and a big bag. Tom was curious, so he followed the man from street to street, corner to corner.

The old man eventually stopped at a park. Tom was so excited that he couldn't help but meow! The old man looked a little confused. He didn't hear Tom meowing because he was deaf.

Then, the old man opened his bag, and there was a stack of treats inside! He showed them to Tom, and Tom ran over and started eating them. Tom was so happy! From that day on, Tom would follow the old man around whenever he could. He knew he could always count on the old man for treats!

The thread seemed to go on forever. It kept winding around, higher and higher into the sky. The bear kept pulling and pulling, amazed at how thin and light the thread was.

Eventually, the thread seemed to get stuck up in the gusts of wind. The bear wiped its eyes again and wondered what to do. Suddenly, something sparkly flew down from the sky. It twirled and spun, before landing right in the bear's paws.

The bear was so happy and surprised! It thought that maybe all its grumpiness had been pushed away by the sparkly thread. It waved goodbye to the thread, thanked it for its help, and started to wander away into the forest.

Lily and Tom were jolly squirrels who liked to play in the park. They liked to run, jump, climb and swing on the trees. They also liked to find nuts and hide them in their nests for winter.

One day, they saw a big pile of nuts under a tree. They ran towards it, excited and hungry. They wanted to eat some nuts and prepare some for later.

"Look, Lily, so many nuts!" Tom said. "Let's take some and share with our friends."

"Good idea, Tom," Lily said. "But we have to be careful. Maybe someone else left them here."

They looked around, but they did not see anyone. They thought it was safe to take some nuts. They picked up some nuts and put them in their mouths. They were crunchy and tasty.

Suddenly, they heard a loud roar. It was a big bear, who was angry and hungry. He had left the nuts there as a trap for other animals. He saw the squirrels and wanted to catch them.

"Hey, you little thieves!" the bear shouted. "Those are my nuts! Give them back or I will eat you!"

Lily and Tom were scared. They dropped the nuts and ran away as fast as they could. They dodged the bear's paws and teeth and climbed up a tree. They hoped the bear would not follow them.

"Phew, that was close!" Tom said. "Are you okay, Lily?"

"I'm okay, Tom," Lily said. "But that was not fun. That was a mean bear. He tricked us with his nuts."

"Yes, he did," Tom said. "But we are smarter than him. We escaped and we still have some nuts in our nests. Let's go back and eat them with our friends."

"Okay, Tom," Lily said. "But next time, let's be more careful. Not all nuts are good nuts."

They nodded and hugged each other. Then they jumped from tree to tree, back to their nests. They were still jolly squirrels, but they learned a lesson. They never took nuts from strangers again.

Mia and Leo were twins who liked to play in the garden. One day, they found a big basket of prunes on the table. Prunes were sweet and soft fruits that they loved to eat.

"Let's have some prunes!" Mia said.

"OK, but we have to ask Mom first," Leo said.

They ran to the kitchen, where Mom was busy cooking. "Mom, can we have some prunes?" they asked.

"Yes, you can, but only one each. The rest are for Grandma, who is coming to visit later. She is very old and needs to eat healthy food. And don't forget to wash your hands before you eat," Mom said.

Mia and Leo nodded and ran back to the table. They each took a prune and washed their hands. They bit into the juicy fruits and smiled.

"These are so good!" Mia said.

"I want another one," Leo said.

"But Mom said only one each," Mia said.

"Mom won't notice. There are so many prunes in the basket. Come on, just one more," Leo said.

He reached for another prune, but Mia stopped him. "No, Leo, that's not fair. We have to share with Grandma. She will be sad if there are no prunes left for her," Mia said.

Leo frowned. He wanted another prune, but he also loved Grandma. He looked at the basket and had an idea. He grabbed a handful of prunes and ran to the shed. He hid the prunes under a pile of old clothes and ran back to the table.

"Where did you go?" Mia asked.

"I just went to the bathroom," Leo lied.

Mia did not believe him. She saw his mouth was purple from the prunes. She was angry and hurt. She decided to tell Mom what Leo did.

She ran to the kitchen, but Mom was not there. She saw a note on the fridge. It said: "I went to the store to buy some milk. I'll be back soon. Love, Mom."

Mia did not know what to do. She wanted to tell Mom, but she also did not want to get Leo in trouble. She felt confused and sad.

She went back to the table and saw that the basket was empty. All the prunes were gone. She gasped. Where did they go?

She heard a loud scream from the shed. It was Leo. She ran to the shed and opened the door. She saw Leo on the floor, surrounded by prunes. He was crying and holding his tummy.

"Mia, help me! I ate too many prunes and now I feel sick. I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I'm sorry!" he sobbed.

Mia felt sorry for Leo. She saw that he was in pain and regretted what he did. She hugged him and said: "It's OK, Leo. I forgive you. But you have to learn to be honest and generous. Prunes are good, but too many can make you sick. And Grandma deserves some too. She loves us and we love her."

Leo nodded. He realized that he was selfish and greedy. He wished he could make the prunes vanish. He said: "You're right, Mia. I'm sorry. I love you and Grandma. Can you help me put the prunes back in the basket?"

Mia smiled. She said: "Of course, Leo. Let's do it together. And then we can wait for Mom and Grandma and tell them the truth. Maybe they will still let us have one more prune each, if we say sorry and promise to be good."

They picked up the prunes and put them back in the basket. They carried the basket to the table and waited for Mom and Grandma. They felt better and hoped that they would still love them.

The moral of the story is: Honesty and generosity are better than selfishness and greed.

One day, a hero went to the forest to look for a rare flower. He wanted to give it to his friend who was sick. He walked and walked until he saw a bright red flower with many petals. He was happy and reached out to pick it.

But the flower was sharp! It hurt his hand and made it bleed. He cried out in pain and dropped the flower. Then he heard a voice.

"I'm sorry, fairy. I didn't know it was your flower. I wanted to give it to my friend who is sick. He likes red flowers and they are rare in our town." The hero said.

The fairy looked at the hero's hand and felt sorry for him. She said, "I see. You are a kind hero who cares for your friend. But you should not take things that are not yours without asking. That is wrong and can hurt you and others."

The hero nodded and said, "You are right, fairy. I'm sorry I was rude and greedy. Can you forgive me and help me heal my hand?"

The fairy smiled and said, "Yes, I forgive you and I will help you. But you have to promise me something. You have to promise me that you will respect nature and ask before you take anything from it. And you have to promise me that you will share your kindness with others and help them when they need it."

The hero agreed and said, "I promise, fairy. Thank you for your forgiveness and help. You are a wise and good fairy."

The fairy touched the hero's hand with her magic and healed it. Then she gave him another red flower that was not sharp. She said, "This is for your friend. I hope he gets well soon. Lily was happy to hear that and they went to the toy doctor. The toy doctor said that Teddy needed an operation to fix his arm. The operation was very cheap and Lily's mommy was happy about that. 

After the operation, Teddy was all better and Lily was so happy. She hugged Teddy tightly and said, "Thank you, toy doctor! You fixed Teddy's arm!" 

The toy doctor smiled and said, "You're welcome, Lily. Now Teddy can play with you again." 

Lily and Teddy went home, but before they left, Lily paused and turned back to the toy doctor. "Thank you again, toy doctor. You're the best!" she said. 

The toy doctor smiled and waved goodbye as Lily and Teddy walked out the door, happy and content.

Soon another bird landed in the garden and the other two birds began to fight. Anna realized the new bird was the same color as the one that shouted it. Anna thought the new bird must be jealous that it didn't have its own corner of the garden.

Anna watched as the birds fought until, finally, the older bird sent the new one away. As the new bird flew away, the older bird looked happier and Anna knew it must be happy to have the garden all to itself. Anna laughed and decided to find her own place to play in the garden.

The new boy pushed the merry-go-round hard. He jumped on and twisted. He smiled and said, "This is fun. I am the best." He did not see the loose screw on the handle. He did not hear the creaking sound. He did not feel the handle break.

The merry-go-round spun out of control. The new boy flew off and landed on the ground. He hit his chest hard. He could not breathe. He felt a sharp pain in his lung. He cried and called for help. But no one came. The park was empty.

Sam and Lily saw what happened. They felt sorry for the new boy. They ran to him and asked, "Are you okay?" The new boy shook his head. He said, "No. I can't breathe. I need a doctor." Sam and Lily nodded. They said, "We will help you. We will call for help." They ran to the phone and dialed 911. They hoped the new boy would be okay. They learned a lesson. They learned to share and be kind. They learned to twist carefully.

Sara and Ben were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They also made a snow fort and some snowballs.

"Let's pretend we are king and queen of the snow," Sara said. "You can be the king and I can be the queen."

"OK," Ben said. "But we need a crown and a scepter."

They looked around and saw a shiny icicle hanging from a tree. It sparkled in the sun.

"I have an idea," Sara said. "We can use the icicle as a scepter. It is icy and pretty."

She reached for the icicle, but it was too high. She jumped and stretched, but she could not touch it.

"Help me, Ben," she said. "You are taller than me. You can pull the icicle down."

Ben nodded and went to the tree. He grabbed the icicle and pulled hard. But the icicle was stuck and did not move.

"Pull harder, Ben," Sara said. "You can do it."

Ben pulled harder and harder. He felt the icicle wiggle and crack. Then, with a loud snap, the icicle broke off and fell to the ground.

"Yay, we did it," Sara said. "Now we have a scepter for our queen."

She picked up the icicle and held it in her hand. It was cold and wet. She smiled and waved it in the air.

"Look at me, Ben," she said. "I am the queen of the snow. And you are my king."

Ben smiled and put the hat on his head. He took Sara's hand and they walked to their snow fort.

They were happy and had fun. They were the king and queen of the snow.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play with toys and books and animals. One day, they went to the library with their moms. They saw a big book with many pictures of different countries. Lily and Ben wanted to see the book.

"Can we look at the book, please?" Lily asked her mom.

"Look, Lily! This country is so amazing! It has sand and pyramids and camels!" Ben said.

Lily looked at the picture and felt envious. She wanted to see the book too. She grabbed the book from Ben and turned the page. They both saw a country with green and flowers and rainbows. They smiled and showed it to each other.

"Look, Ben and Lily! This country is so beautiful! It has green and flowers and rainbows!" they said together.

They looked at each other and laughed. They realized they did not have to be envious. They could share the book and see all the countries. They hugged and said sorry.

"Sorry, Lily. I should not have grabbed the book from you," Ben said.

"Sorry, Ben. I should not have grabbed the book from you," Lily said.

They took turns to look at the book and learn about the countries. They had fun and thanked their moms for taking them to the library. They were still best friends.

Tom and Lily liked to play chess with their dad. Chess was a game with black and white pieces that moved on a board with squares. Dad taught them how to play and they had fun.

One day, Tom and Lily saw some flowers in the garden. They were very pretty and had many colors. They smelled good too. Tom and Lily wanted to pick some flowers for their mom.

"Look, Lily, these flowers are blooming!" Tom said. "They are so bright and happy. Let's pick some for mom. She will love them."

"Okay, Tom, but we have to be careful. We can't pick too many or hurt the plants." Lily said. "We have to share with the bees and the butterflies. They need the flowers too."

Tom and Lily picked some flowers, but not too many. They made a nice bouquet and ran to the house. They wanted to surprise their mom.

But when they got to the house, they saw their dad playing chess by himself. He had taken all the black and white pieces and put them on his side of the board. He looked bored and unhappy.

"Dad, what are you doing?" Tom asked. "Why are you playing chess by yourself? Where are our pieces?"

"I'm sorry, kids, but I wanted to play chess and you were not here." Dad said. "So I took all the pieces and played by myself. It's not as fun as playing with you, but I was selfish and didn't want to wait."

Tom and Lily felt sad and angry. They thought their dad was not fair and not nice. They loved chess, but they also loved flowers and their mom. They wanted to play with their dad, but they also wanted to share with the nature.

"Dad, that's not how you play chess." Lily said. "You have to share the pieces and take turns. You can't play by yourself. That's not fun. That's selfish."

Tom and Lily gave their dad the bouquet of flowers. They hoped he would see how beautiful and generous they were. They hoped he would say sorry and play chess with them again.

"Dad, these are for you." Tom said. "We picked some flowers for mom, but we want to share with you too. We love you, dad, but we don't like it when you are selfish. Please play chess with us again. Please share and be fair."

Dad looked at the flowers and felt ashamed. He realized he had been selfish and rude. He hugged Tom and Lily and thanked them for the flowers. He said sorry and asked them to forgive him. He put back the pieces on the board and invited them to play chess with him. He promised to share and be fair.

Tom and Lily smiled and forgave their dad. They were happy to play chess with him again. They also gave some flowers to their mom and told her they loved her. They learned that chess and flowers were both good, but only if they shared them with others. They learned that being selfish was not fun, but being kind and generous was.

Lily and Max are twins. They share a room and a bed. Lily likes to sleep with her teddy bear. Max likes to sleep with his truck. One night, Lily and Max have a problem.

"Max, your truck is poking my nose!" Lily says. She tries to move away from the hard toy.

"Sorry, Lily, but I need my truck. It makes me feel safe," Max says. He hugs his truck closer to his chest.

"But it hurts, Max. And it is noisy. It goes vroom vroom in my ear," Lily says. She is angry and sad.

"Too bad, Lily. This is my side of the bed. You have your teddy bear. He is soft and quiet," Max says. He is stubborn and proud.

Lily and Max do not talk to each other. They turn their backs and try to sleep. But it is difficult. Lily's nose is sore and Max's truck is cold. They miss each other. They want to say sorry. But they do not know how.

Then, they hear a voice. It is their mom. She comes to check on them. She sees them lying apart. She smiles and has an idea.

"Hello, my sweeties. How are you?" she says. She sits on the bed and strokes their hair.

"Not good, mom. Max's truck is mean. It pokes my nose and makes noise," Lily says.

"Not good, mom. Lily's teddy bear is boring. It is soft and quiet," Max says.

"I see. Well, maybe you can try something new. How about you swap your toys for one night? Maybe you will like them better," mom says.

Lily and Max look at each other. They are curious and surprised. They think about it. Then, they nod and smile.

"Okay, mom. Let's try it," they say.

They give each other their toys. Lily holds Max's truck. Max holds Lily's teddy bear. They cuddle them and say thank you.

"Good night, my sweeties. I love you," mom says. She kisses them and turns off the light.

Lily and Max snuggle closer. They feel warm and happy. They whisper good night. They sleep. It is easy.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to travel with their mom and dad. They went to many places and saw many things. One day, they went to a big park with many trees and flowers. They saw a pond with ducks and fish. They saw a playground with swings and slides. They saw a picnic area with tables and benches.

"Let's have lunch here," mom said. "We have sandwiches and juice and cookies."

"Yay!" Anna and Ben said. They ran to a table and sat down. Mom and dad gave them their food and drinks. They ate and talked and laughed.

After lunch, mom and dad said they wanted to rest for a while. They told Anna and Ben to play nearby, but not to go too far. They also told them not to touch anything that could hurt them, like fire or sharp things.

"OK," Anna and Ben said. They promised to be good and careful. They took their toys and went to the playground. They had fun on the swings and slides. They made friends with other kids. They were happy.

But then, Anna saw something shiny in the grass. It was a spark. It came from a small box that someone had left behind. Anna was curious. She wanted to see what was inside the box. She left her toys and walked towards the spark.

"Anna, where are you going?" Ben asked. He saw his sister leaving the playground. He followed her.

"I want to see what this is," Anna said. She pointed to the box. She picked it up and opened it.

"Anna, don't!" Ben said. He remembered what mom and dad had said. He was scared.

But it was too late. As soon as Anna opened the box, a loud noise and a bright flash came out. It was a firework. It exploded in Anna's hand. Anna screamed. She dropped the box and the firework. She felt pain in her hand. She cried.

Ben ran to her and hugged her. He tried to calm her down. He looked at her hand. It was red and swollen. He was worried.

"Anna, are you OK?" he asked.

"No, it hurts!" Anna said. She sobbed.

Mom and dad heard the noise and the cry. They ran to their kids. They saw what had happened. They were shocked and angry.

"Anna, Ben, what did you do?" mom asked.

"We're sorry, mom," Ben said. He told her what Anna had done. He said he had tried to stop her, but he was too late.

Mom and dad took Anna to a nearby nurse. The nurse looked at Anna's hand. She said it was a burn. She put some cream and a bandage on it. She said it would heal, but it would take time. She said Anna had to be careful and not touch the burn.

"Thank you, nurse," mom and dad said. They thanked the nurse for her help. They took Anna and Ben back to the car. They decided to end their trip and go home.

On the way home, mom and dad talked to Anna and Ben. They said they were glad they were not hurt worse. They said they loved them very much. But they also said they were disappointed and sad. They said they had broken their promise and their trust. They said they had been naughty and foolish. They said they had to learn from their mistake and not do it again.

"We're sorry, mom and dad," Anna and Ben said. They felt ashamed and sorry. They said they had learned their lesson and they would not do it again.

Mom and dad hugged them and kissed them. They said they forgave them and they were proud of them. They said they hoped they would still enjoy traveling and exploring, but they also hoped they would be more careful and obedient.

Anna and Ben nodded and smiled. They said they loved mom and dad and they thanked them for their trip. They said they still liked traveling and exploring, but they also said they would be more careful and obedient. They said they would never touch a spark or a firework again.

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the value of being careful and obedient, and the consequences of being curious and reckless. It also teaches the value of being honest and repentant, and the forgiveness and love of parents.

Ben sees the bird and gets scared. He grabs Sam's hand and runs away. They leave their rockets behind.

Sam and Ben hide behind a bush. They are sad and scared. They lost their rockets. They worked hard to improve them. They want them back.

"Maybe we can get them later, when the bird is gone," Sam says.

"Maybe," Ben says. "But I don't want to play with rockets anymore. They are too dangerous."

"Me neither," Sam says. "Let's play with something else. Something safe and fun."

They think for a while. Then they smile.

"Let's play with bubbles!" they say.

They run back to their house and get their bubble wands and soap. They blow bubbles in the air and watch them float and pop. They laugh and giggle.

They forget about the rockets and the bird. They are happy and safe. They have fun with bubbles.

"I'm glad you like them, sweetie," her mom said. "But it's time for bed now. You need to sleep."

"But I want to watch the stars, mom," Lily said. "Please, can I stay up a little longer?"

"No, Lily, you have to sleep," her mom said. "The stars will be here tomorrow night, too. Come on, let me tuck you in."

Lily was not happy. She did not want to sleep. She wanted to watch the stars. She thought of a plan. She waited until her mom left the room, and then she got up and opened the curtain a little bit. She hoped that the moonlight would make the stars glow brighter.

But she made a mistake. The moonlight was too bright, and it made the stars fade. Lily could not see them anymore. She was sad and angry. She tried to close the curtain again, but she pulled too hard and the curtain fell down. She heard a loud noise and her mom came back.

"Lily, what are you doing?" her mom asked. "Why did you open the curtain and pull it down?"

"I'm sorry, mom," Lily said. "I wanted to see the stars, but they went away. I tried to fix it, but I made it worse."

Her mom sighed and hugged her. "It's okay, Lily. I know you love the stars, but you have to follow the rules. You can't open the curtain at night, and you can't pull it down. You could hurt yourself or break something. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded. She felt sorry for what she did. She realized that her mom was right. She needed to sleep, and the stars would be there tomorrow night. She said sorry again and hugged her mom back.

Her mom smiled and kissed her. "I love you, Lily. And I love your stars, too. They are very beautiful. But they need to rest, too, just like you. Let's put the curtain back and turn off the light. Maybe you can dream of the stars tonight."

Lily agreed. She helped her mom put the curtain back and turned off the light. She lay down in her bed and looked at the stars. They were glowing again, softly and gently. She felt calm and happy. She said good night to her mom and the stars, and closed her eyes. She fell asleep, dreaming of the stars.

Mom said, "We need some flour, some sugar, some eggs, and some milk. Can you help me find them?" Lily nodded and looked around the kitchen. She saw the flour on the shelf, the sugar in the jar, the eggs in the fridge, and the milk in the carton. She pointed to each one and said, "There, there, there, and there!"

Mom said, "Good job, Lily! Now we need to measure them. Do you know how to use a teaspoon?" Lily shook her head and said, "No, Mom. What is a teaspoon?" Mom showed her a small silver spoon and said, "This is a teaspoon. We use it to measure small amounts of things, like sugar or salt. Can you hold it for me?" Lily took the teaspoon and held it in her hand. It felt light and shiny.

Mom said, "Now we need four teaspoons of sugar. Can you count with me?" Lily said, "Yes, Mom!" She scooped some sugar with the teaspoon and poured it into the bowl. She said, "One!" She did it again and said, "Two!" She did it two more times and said, "Three! Four!" Mom said, "Well done, Lily! You are a great helper!"

Lily felt happy and proud. She asked, "What do we do next, Mom?" Mom said, "We need to crack the eggs and whisk them with the milk. Do you want to try?" Lily said, "Yes, Mom!" She picked up an egg and tapped it on the edge of the bowl. It cracked and spilled. Lily said, "Oops!" Mom said, "That's okay, Lily. It happens sometimes. Just be careful not to get any shells in the bowl." Lily tried again and cracked another egg. She said, "Like this, Mom?" Mom said, "Yes, like this, Lily. You are doing great!"

Lily cracked two more eggs and poured the milk into the bowl. Mom gave her a whisk and said, "Now we need to mix them together. Can you whisk them for me?" Lily said, "Yes, Mom!" She moved the whisk back and forth in the bowl. She saw the eggs and the milk become one. She said, "Wow, Mom! It's changing!" Mom said, "That's right, Lily. It's becoming a batter. That's what we need to make the cake."

Lily asked, "Can we add some chocolate, Mom?" Mom said, "Sure, Lily. We can add some chocolate chips. Do you like chocolate?" Lily said, "Yes, Mom! I love chocolate!" Mom said, "Me too, Lily. Me too." She opened a bag of chocolate chips and said, "Can you sprinkle some on top of the batter?" Lily said, "Yes, Mom!" She grabbed a handful of chocolate chips and sprinkled them on the batter. She said, "Yummy, Mom! It looks good!"

Mom said, "It does look good, Lily. You are a wonderful baker. Now we need to put the batter in a pan and bake it in the oven. Do you know how to do that?" Lily said, "No, Mom. How do we do that?" Mom said, "I'll show you, Lily. But first, we need to preheat the oven. Do you know what that means?" Lily said, "No, Mom. What does that mean?" Mom said, "It means we need to make the oven hot before we put the cake in. Can you help me turn on the oven?" Lily said, "Yes, Mom!" She followed Mom to the oven and watched her turn a knob. She said, "What does that do, Mom?" Mom said, "It sets the temperature, Lily. We need to make it 350 degrees. Do you know what that means?" Lily said, "No, Mom. What does that mean?" Mom said, "It means it's very hot, Lily. So hot that it can cook the cake. But we have to be careful not to touch it, because it can burn us. Do you understand?" Lily said, "Yes, Mom. I understand. We don't touch the oven. We only look at it." Mom said, "That's right, Lily. We only look at it. And we wait for it to beep. Do you know what that means?" Lily said, "No, Mom. What does that mean?" Mom said, "It means it's ready, Lily. Ready to bake the cake. Do you want to hear it beep?"

The old lady was outraged that someone had thrown away something so valuable and decided to burn it to teach the perpetrator a lesson.

A little girl was playing in the nearby field and she noticed the smoke. She screamed, "Mama, there's a fire!" Her mother rushed to the scene and saw the old lady tending to the fire.

The woman asked, "What are you doing?"

The old lady replied, "Burning this filthy round log - someone threw it away and I want to show them that was a mistake!" 

The woman agreed and she and her daughter were amazed at the bright and warm flames.

"Wow, look at this!" Lila says. "It is a light. Maybe it can make wishes."

Tom picks up the lamp and rubs it. Nothing happens. He rubs it harder. Still nothing.

"Maybe it is dirty," Lila says. "We need to polish it."

They find a cloth and some water. They start to polish the lamp. They make it very clean and bright. They hope it will work.

Suddenly, a puff of smoke comes out of the lamp. A man appears. He has a big smile and a long beard. He wears a turban and a robe.

"Hello, hello!" he says. "I am the genie of the lamp. You have freed me from the box. I am very happy. I will grant you three wishes. Anything you want, I can do. What do you wish for?"

Lila and Tom are surprised and excited. They look at each other. They have so many ideas. They wonder what to choose.

"Can we have more toys?" Tom asks.

"Can we have a pony?" Lila asks.

The genie nods. "Of course, of course. Those are easy wishes. I can make them happen. But you have to be careful. You only have one wish left. You have to make it a good one. Think hard. What do you really want?"

Lila and Tom think hard. They have more toys and a pony. They are very happy. But they also want something else. Something more important.

They whisper to each other. They agree on their last wish. They look at the genie and say together:

"We wish for our mommy and daddy to be happy and healthy. And we wish for you to be free and happy too."

The genie smiles. He is touched by their wish. He says:

"That is a very good wish. A very kind wish. I will make it happen. Your mommy and daddy will be happy and healthy. And I will be free and happy too. Thank you, thank you. You are very good children. I will always remember you. Goodbye, goodbye."

He snaps his fingers. The lamp disappears. The genie disappears. Lila and Tom hug each other. They run to their mommy and daddy. They tell them everything. They show them their toys and their pony. They are all happy and healthy. And they live happily ever after.

"And this is my nation. It is called China. It is far and big and has many people," Sue says.

But then, Tim sees a nation he does not like. It is called France. It is small and has a funny shape. Tim thinks it is silly.

"I do not like this nation. It is bad and ugly. I will bite it," Tim says.

He opens his mouth and tries to bite the map. Sue is shocked and angry.

"No, Tim, no! You cannot bite the map. That is rude and mean. You will hurt the map and the people in the nation. You have to be nice and respectful," Sue says.

She pulls the map away from Tim and scolds him. Tim feels ashamed and sorry. He realizes he was wrong.

"I am sorry, Sue. I was silly and mean. I will not bite the map again. I will be nice and respectful. I want to learn more about the nations and the people. Can you teach me?" Tim says.

Sue smiles and forgives him. She is happy that Tim learned his lesson. She teaches him more about the nations and the people. They share their stories and cultures. They become better friends.

The moral of the story is: Do not bite what you do not like. Be nice and respectful to others. Learn from your mistakes and grow.

Jessie thought that was a good idea, so she waited and waited. Finally, the sunny day was over and the frog was nice and dry. She picked up the cute frog and took it home.

The frog was now her best friend. Every day they went out and explored the wild together. It was so much fun! 

From then on, Jessie and her loyal frog had many charming adventures in the wild.

They heard a whistle. It was really loud and came from the trees. "What is that?" Sophie asked. Daddy said, "I think it's a bird. It's whistling for a friend."

Sophie kept walking and they soon came to a pepper bush. Daddy gave Sophie a pepper. It was red and spicy! Sophie smiled and thanked Daddy.

Then they heard a noise. It sounded like a bark. Daddy looked worried so they went back home.

When they got home, Daddy was still worried. He said that barking must have been a wolf!

Sophie felt safe in her home. She snuggled up with Daddy and sure enough, everything was okay.

Once upon a time there were two friends called Amy and Jack. One day, they decided to go for a walk in the park. As they were walking, Jack suddenly noticed a big well.

He asked Amy if they could explore it. Amy was hesitant but agreed.
They walked up to the well and Jack asked Amy if he could look down inside it. Amy replied, "No. It's not safe."

Jack wouldn't give up though. He said, "But I'm fit, I can climb down easily."

Amy looked around nervously before replying "No, it's too dangerous. We need to go."

Jack wasn't happy about this reply and said, "But why can't I climb down into the well? Why can't we have a look?"

Amy paused for a moment before saying calmly, "It's not safe, Jack. We need to find something else to do." 

Jack was still not satisfied but he closed his mouth and followed Amy away from the well. They found a lot of other fun things to do in the park that day and they both had a really great time.

Suddenly she saw a fox on the ground. The bird was very scared.

"Don't be afraid," said the fox. "I promise I won't hurt you. I'm just looking for a snack."

The bird replied to the fox, "But I'm too small to be a snack."

The fox said, "That's okay, I'm looking for something bigger anyway. You can stay here, I will be on my way."

The bird thanked the fox and flew to the very top of the tree. She felt safe and happily nested in the top of the tree. And, that is how the humble little bird found a place to stay, just by taking a peek.

"Grandma, what is this word?" Lily asked, pointing to the word.

"That is a spell, my dear. A good spell that makes the pie taste delicious and brings us luck," Grandma said, smiling.

"A spell? How do you make a spell?" Lily asked, curious.

"Well, you need to use special words that have magic in them, and say them with your heart. Like this: 'Pie, pie, sweet and nice, fill our bellies with delight, bless our home with love and light,'" Grandma said, and then kissed the dough.

Lily was amazed and wanted to try it too. She looked at the dough and tried to say the words, but she got them wrong.

"Pie, pie, neat and rice, fill our bellies with mice, bless our home with glove and bite," Lily said, and then giggled.

Grandma laughed too, and hugged Lily. "That was a very funny spell, my dear, but not a very good one. You need to practice more, and learn how to read and write the words. But I love you anyway, and I'm sure the pie will be yummy," Grandma said.

Sam and Mia ran to the turkey and tried to pet it and give it food. The turkey was friendly and ate from their hands. But then, Sam had an idea. He took out the red car from his bag and said to Mia, "Let's zoom the car near the turkey and see what it does. It will be fun!"

"OK, Tom, but be quick. We don't want to get lost in the forest," Lily said.

They kicked the ball and chased it, but they did not notice that they were going deeper and deeper into the forest. They also did not notice that a big bear was following them, smelling their scent. The bear was hungry and angry, and it wanted to eat them.

The ball rolled to a big tree, and Tom and Lily ran to get it. They were about to kick it again, when they heard a loud roar behind them. They turned around and saw the bear, standing on its hind legs, showing its sharp teeth and claws.

"Help, Lily, a bear!" Tom screamed. "Run, run, run!"

They dropped the ball and ran as fast as they could, but the bear was faster. It was about to catch them, when they saw a man with a gun. The man was a hunter, and he had heard their screams. He aimed his gun at the bear and shot it. The bear fell to the ground, and the man ran to Tom and Lily.

"Are you OK, kids?" the man asked. "What are you doing here? This forest is dangerous. There are many wild animals that can hurt you."

"We're sorry, sir," Tom said. "We saw a ball and we wanted to play with it. We didn't mean to leave the path."

"We're sorry, too," Lily said. "We were silly and we forgot to be careful."

The man rubbed their heads and smiled. "It's OK, kids. I'm glad you're safe. But you have to promise me something. Never go into the forest alone again. Always stay with your parents or someone who can protect you. And always listen to your parents when they tell you what to do and what not to do. Do you understand?"

"Yes, sir, we understand," Tom and Lily said. "We promise. Thank you for saving us."

The man took them by the hand and led them back to the path. He gave them back their ball and told them to go home. Tom and Lily hugged him and thanked him again. Then they ran home, holding their ball and each other. They learned their lesson and never went into the forest alone again.

The moral of the story is: Be careful and listen to your parents.

Sara hugged Mia and said, "Don't be scared, sister. I can help you."

Mia smiled and said, "How can you help me, Sara? You are too little to know the test."

Sara said, "I can help you by being your friend. We can discuss the test and make it fun. I can ask you questions and you can tell me the answers. I can draw pictures and you can write words. We can sing songs and make jokes. We can play and learn together."

Mia thought for a moment and said, "That sounds nice, Sara. Thank you for being my friend. Maybe you are not too little to know the test. Maybe you are very smart and kind."

Sara and Mia hugged and started to discuss the test. They had fun and learned a lot. They were not lonely anymore. They were happy sisters.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toy animals in the garden. They had a lot of animals, but their favorite was the big rhinoceros. It was gray and had a thick horn on its nose. They liked to pretend it was a real rhinoceros and make loud noises.

"Roar!" Ben said, holding the rhinoceros in his hand. "I am the king of the animals. No one can stop me!"

"Stop, stop!" Lily said, holding a toy giraffe. "You are not the king. You are mean. You have to share the animals with me."

"No, I don't!" Ben said, pushing Lily away. "The rhinoceros is mine. It is the best animal. Go away!"

Lily was sad and angry. She wanted to play with the rhinoceros too. She had an idea. She ran to the house and came back with a cloth and a bottle. She said to Ben, "I have something for you. It is a magic polish. It can make your rhinoceros shiny and pretty. Do you want to try it?"

Ben was curious. He liked shiny and pretty things. He said, "Yes, I want to try it. Give it to me."

Lily gave him the cloth and the bottle. She said, "You have to rub the cloth on the rhinoceros with the polish. Then it will sparkle."

Ben opened the bottle and poured some polish on the cloth. He rubbed it on the rhinoceros. But something was wrong. The polish was not magic. It was sticky and smelly. It made the rhinoceros dirty and ugly. It also made Ben's hand dirty and smelly.

"Yuck!" Ben said, dropping the rhinoceros. "What is this? This is not polish. This is bad. You tricked me!"

Lily laughed. She said, "Yes, I tricked you. This is not polish. This is honey. You were mean to me, so I was mean to you. Now you have to wash your hand and the rhinoceros. And you have to share the animals with me."

Ben was mad. He said, "No, I don't! You are meaner than me. I don't want to play with you anymore. Go away!"

Lily said, "Fine. I don't want to play with you either. I will take the giraffe and the other animals. You can keep the rhinoceros. It is not the best animal. It is the worst animal."

Lily and Ben went to different sides of the garden. They did not talk to each other. They were not happy. They missed playing with each other. They wished they had not been mean. They wished they had shared the animals. They wished they had used real polish.

Anna was curious. She liked surprises. Maybe Tom was being nice today. She opened the door a little bit.

"What is it?" she asked.

"Ha ha ha! You look funny!" Tom laughed. He ran away before Anna could say anything.

Anna was angry and sad. She looked at her dress and her hair. They were ruined. She looked at her bulb. It was covered with tomato sauce too. It was not bright anymore.

She started to cry. She did not like Tom. He was mean and rude. He spoiled her dancing. She wished he would leave her alone. She did not trust him anymore.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play with toys. One day, they saw a big toy shop with many toys in the window. They asked their mom if they could go inside and look.

"Okay, but we can only buy one toy each," their mom said. "You have to choose carefully and share with each other."

Tim and Sam were enthusiastic and ran into the toy shop. They saw cars, trains, dolls, puzzles, and many other toys. Tim saw a big globe that showed the earth with different colors and shapes. He thought it was very cool and wanted to learn more about it.

"Mom, can I buy this globe?" he asked.

Sam saw a shiny robot that could make noises and move. He thought it was very fun and wanted to play with it.

"Mom, can I buy this robot?" he asked.

Their mom looked at the price tags and saw that the globe and the robot were very expensive. She shook her head and said, "No, these toys are too much money. You have to find something cheaper and smaller."

Tim and Sam were sad and disappointed. They did not want to give up their toys. They started to argue and fight over who could have the globe or the robot.

"Stop it, both of you!" their mom said. "You are being selfish and greedy. You have to be grateful for what you have and think of others. There are many children who have no toys at all. How would you feel if you were them?"

Tim and Sam felt ashamed and sorry. They realized that their mom was right and that they were being bad. They apologized to their mom and to each other. They decided to put back the globe and the robot and look for something else.

They found a box of crayons and a coloring book that had pictures of the earth and its animals. They thought it was nice and interesting. They agreed to buy it and share it. They also found a small teddy bear that was soft and cute. They thought it was a good gift for their baby sister. They asked their mom if they could buy these two things.

Their mom smiled and nodded. She was proud of them for being kind and generous. She paid for the crayons, the coloring book, and the teddy bear. She gave them a hug and a kiss.

"Thank you, mom," Tim and Sam said.

"You're welcome, my boys," their mom said. "You made a good choice. I hope you enjoy your toys and learn something new. And remember, the best things in life are not things, but love and friendship."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the value of gratitude, sharing, and caring for others. It also shows the importance of learning and curiosity.

"Can we eat it now?" Tom asks.

"Not yet. We have to wait for mom. She will tell us when it is ready," Sam says.

"What are you cooking, boys?" she asks.

"We are cooking a bulb. We found it in the garden. We want to eat it," Sam says.

Mom smiles. She is proud of her clever sons. She tastes the bulb. It is soft and sweet.

"You did a good job, boys. This is a turnip. It is a healthy and tasty vegetable. You can eat it with some butter and bread," she says.

She serves them some turnip and bread. They eat it and enjoy it. They are happy. They thank mom and hug her.

The end.

But then they hear a voice. It is Mom. She is coming to the kitchen. She says, "Who opened the fridge? What are you doing with the cake?"

Tim and Kim are scared. They know Mom will be angry. They try to hide the cake. But it is too big. They drop the cake on the floor. The cake breaks into pieces. The frosting and sprinkles make a mess.

Mom sees the cake on the floor. She is very angry. She says, "Tim and Kim, you are terrible! You ruined the cake! The cake was for Grandma's birthday! How could you do this?"

Tim and Kim feel bad. They say, "We are sorry, Mom. We did not know. We were hungry. We wanted to eat the cake."

Mom says, "You should not eat the cake. The cake is not for you. The cake is for Grandma. You should prevent yourself from taking things that are not yours. You should ask before you eat. You should be good and polite."

Tim and Kim nod. They say, "We understand, Mom. We will not do it again. We will be good and polite. We will help you clean the mess. We will say sorry to Grandma. We will make her a new cake."

Mom sighs. She says, "Thank you, Tim and Kim. I love you, but you need to learn. Now, let's clean the mess and make a new cake. Maybe Grandma will forgive us."

Tim and Kim hug Mom. They say, "We love you, Mom. We will learn. We will make Grandma happy."

One day, they saw a big dog in the park. The dog was barking and running after a ball. Tom and Lily were scared of the dog. They ran away from the dog and hid behind a tree.

"Tom, I am worried. What if the dog finds us and bites us?" Lily said.

"Don't worry, Lily. We are safe here. The dog is not bad. He just wants to play with his ball. He will not hurt us." Tom said.

"How do you know that, Tom?" Lily asked.

"Because my dad told me. He has a lot of wisdom. He knows a lot of things. He said dogs are our friends, not our enemies. We just have to be nice to them and they will be nice to us." Tom said.

"Really? Are you sure?" Lily said.

"Yes, I am sure. Come on, let's go and say hello to the dog. Maybe he will let us play with his ball too." Tom said.

Tom and Lily came out from behind the tree. They walked slowly and gently towards the dog. The dog saw them and wagged his tail. He dropped his ball and licked their faces. Tom and Lily laughed and petted the dog. They played with him and his ball. They were not scared anymore. They were very fast and happy.

Anna and Ben were on a big boat with their mom and dad. They wanted to see the fish and the coral in the water. Mom and dad gave them masks and tubes to breathe. They said, "Be careful and stay close to us. The reef is very beautiful, but also very sharp. And remember, don't touch anything with your hands."

Anna and Ben nodded and jumped into the water. They saw many colors and shapes under the water. They saw yellow fish, blue fish, red fish, and even a big green turtle. They followed the turtle as it swam slowly. They were very happy and excited.

But then, Ben saw something shiny and round on the reef. He wanted to see what it was. He swam closer and closer, and reached out his hand to touch it. But he did not see the sharp coral that was next to it. He cut his finger and it hurt a lot. He cried out, "Ow, ow, ow!"

Anna heard him and swam back to him. She saw his finger bleeding and said, "Ben, what did you do? Mom and dad told us not to touch anything. Come on, let's go back to the boat. They will help you."

Ben felt sorry and scared. He said, "I'm sorry, Anna. I just wanted to see what it was. It looked like a shiny ball. But it was not a ball. It was a flexible star. A starfish. Look, it is moving its arms." He showed her the starfish that was still in his hand.

Anna looked at the starfish and said, "Wow, it is very pretty. But you have to let it go, Ben. It belongs to the reef. And you have to be more careful next time. Remember, the reef is very beautiful, but also very sharp." She took the starfish from his hand and gently put it back on the reef. Then she took his hand and said, "Come on, let's go back to the boat. Mom and dad will make your finger better. And then we can see more fish and turtles. OK?"

Ben nodded and said, "OK, Anna. Thank you for helping me. You are a good sister. I love you."

Anna smiled and said, "I love you too, Ben. And I love the reef. It is very beautiful." They swam back to the boat, holding hands.

Lily was a little girl who loved flowers. She liked to pick them and smell them and make them into crowns. She had a special flower that she planted in a pot. It was a sunflower. She watered it every day and waited for it to grow.

One morning, she saw a yellow bud on the stem. She was so happy. She ran to tell her mom and dad. They came to see the flower and smiled. They said it would bloom soon and be very big and bright. Lily hugged them and thanked them for the seed.

The next day, Lily woke up early and ran to the window. She saw the sunflower had opened its petals. It was as big as her head and as bright as the sun. She clapped her hands and sang a song. She sang about the sunflower and how much she loved it. She sang so loud that the birds heard her and joined in. They flew to the flower and perched on its leaves. They sang their own songs and made a beautiful chorus.

Lily felt very happy. She grabbed her hat and ran outside. She wanted to see the sunflower up close and touch its soft petals. She wanted to hear the birds and their songs. She wanted to share her joy with the flower. She reached the pot and leaned in. She saw the sunflower had a face. It had two black eyes and a big smile. It looked at her and said hello.

Lily was surprised. She had never heard a flower talk before. She said hello back and asked its name. The sunflower said its name was Sunny. It said it was glad to meet her and thanked her for taking care of it. It said it liked her song and wanted to hear more. It asked her to sing with it and the birds.

Lily smiled and nodded. She felt a deep friendship with Sunny and the birds. She felt like they were her family. She sang with them and laughed with them. She felt the sun on her face and the wind in her hair. She felt the flower in her heart. She felt very happy. She felt like she was blooming too.

Tim and Sam are scared. They think the record player is a real crocodile. They run away and hide behind the sofa.

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to help their dad. Their dad was a carpenter who made things from wood. He made tables, chairs, beds, and toys. He sold them to people who needed them. He was very good at his work and very reliable. People trusted him and paid him well.

One day, their dad had to go to the town to buy some more wood. He asked Tom and Sam to watch his shop and sell his things. He said, "Be honest and fair with the customers. Don't ask for too much money or too little. And don't sell anything that is broken or not finished. I will be back soon."

Tom and Sam agreed and said goodbye to their dad. They waited for the customers to come. Soon, a lady came and looked at a toy horse. She liked it and asked, "How much is this toy horse?"

Tom said, "It is five coins, ma'am. It is very nice and strong. My dad made it with care."

The lady said, "That is a fair price. I will buy it for my son. He loves horses."

She gave Tom five coins and took the toy horse. Tom thanked her and put the coins in a jar.

Sam saw this and felt jealous. He wanted to have more money than Tom. He thought, "If I ask for more money, I can have more coins. Then I can buy more candy and toys for myself."

He saw a man coming and looking at a table. The table was big and sturdy, but it had a small crack on one leg. Sam did not tell the man about the crack. He said, "This table is ten coins, sir. It is very big and sturdy. My dad made it with skill."

The man said, "That is too much for this table. It has a crack on one leg. It is not reliable. It might break."

Sam said, "No, no, sir. The crack is not a problem. It is just a mark of beauty. The table is still reliable. It will not break."

The man did not believe Sam. He said, "You are lying to me. You are trying to cheat me. I will not buy this table. I will go to another shop. And I will tell everyone that you are not honest and fair."

He left the shop and walked away. Sam felt ashamed and scared. He realized that he had done wrong. He had tried to sell something that was broken and not finished. He had asked for too much money. He had lied to the customer. He had not been honest and fair like his dad.

He looked at Tom and saw that he had sold more things and had more coins. He also saw that he had happy customers who thanked him and praised him. He felt sorry and said, "Tom, I am sorry. I was greedy and foolish. I wanted to have more money than you. But I did not sell well. I did not follow dad's words. I lost a customer and a friend. I made dad look bad. Can you forgive me?"

Tom said, "I forgive you, Sam. But you have to learn from your mistake. You have to be honest and fair with the customers. You have to sell what is good and reliable. You have to respect dad's work and reputation. That is how you sell well. That is how you make money and friends. That is how you make dad proud."

Sam nodded and said, "You are right, Tom. I will do better next time. I will be honest and fair. I will sell what is good and reliable. I will respect dad's work and reputation. I will make dad proud."

They hugged and smiled. They waited for their dad to come back. They hoped that he would be happy with their sales. They learned a valuable lesson that day. They learned that honesty and fairness are the best ways to sell well.

But they did not know how to light the candle. They tried to rub it, blow on it, and shake it, but nothing happened. They were sad and confused.

They decided to discuss how to light the candle. They asked each other what they knew about fire and candles. Tom said he saw Mom use a stick with a red tip to light candles. Lily said she saw Dad use a small box with a wheel to make sparks.

They looked around their room for a stick or a box, but they could not find any. They were about to give up, when they heard a knock on the door. It was Mom.

She saw the candle and asked them what they were doing. They told her they wanted to light the candle, but they did not know how. Mom smiled and said she would show them, but only if they promised to be careful and never play with fire without an adult.

She took the candle and the stick and lit the candle. She explained how fire works and why it can be dangerous. She also told them how to blow out the candle and how to be safe around candles.

Tom and Lily thanked Mom and watched the candle with wonder. They liked how it flickered and danced. They felt happy and curious. They forgot about being sad and confused.

Mom was proud of them for being honest and wanting to learn. She was not grumpy at all. She hugged them and said they could keep the candle, but only if they asked her before lighting it again. They agreed and said they loved her.

They all enjoyed the candle together, until it was time for bed. Then they blew out the candle and said good night. They dreamed of fire and candles and learning new things.

Timmy felt better and thanked the bunny for his advice. From that day on, Timmy practiced hopping every day until he became a great hopper, just like the bunny. And they both hopped happily ever after. The end.

On the day of the wedding, everything was perfect. But as they said their vows, Rob couldn't keep the secret any longer. He told Eddie he didn't feel ready and he was sorry but he couldn't get married. Eddie was so sad but agreed. The wedding was stopped and Rob and Eddie said goodbye.

He was grateful for his marriage and for the useful lessons it had taught him.

Once upon a time, there was a little pink rabbit who loved to play in the garden. She especially loved to jump in the mud and roll around. One day, she found a bottle of special ink. It was so pretty and shiny. She looked at it for a long time, wanting to take it home with her.

The rabbit remembered the wise words of her mother, who had always said that taking things that didn't belong to her was wrong. But she really wanted the ink. So, she decided to take it.

The next day, the rabbit put the ink in her pocket and went outside to play. But, soon after, it started to rain and the ink was washed away. Pink ink was everywhere, even in the rabbit's fur!

The rabbit let out a little cry. She thought about how she had taken the ink, even though she knew it didn't belong to her. Now, she would never have it ever again.

The rabbit learned a valuable lesson that day. Just because something might seem pretty and special, it still doesn't mean that it belongs to you. Taking something that doesn't belong to you, no matter how much you want it, is usually wrong.

Anna was curious about what was inside. She opened the dictionary and looked at all the big words. She read some of the words and smiled.

Anna had fun with her dictionary. She shared it with the birds and they looked so happy. Every day she fed the birds and turned the pages.

Anna finally had to leave the park. She hugged her dictionary, gave the birds one last piece of food and went back home.

Anna never forgot about that special smooth book and the birds she fed at the park.

One day, a little girl named Sadie went outside. She gazed at the bright blue sky and saw a fly buzzing around. Sadie smiled and ran after the fly. It flew up and away with Sadie following it. Soon, they were playing tag in the air, with Sadie laughing and the fly zipping around. 

Sadie followed the fly until they reached a big meadow. The flies stopped and Sadie was curious. She carefully walked over to the meadow, where a huge, old tree was standing tall. Sadie gazed up at the tall trunk and saw a bird perched on one of its branches. 

The bird flew away quickly, and Sadie saw something yellow on the ground. She bent down and picked it up - it was a green and yellow leaf, and it was a bit bitter. Sadie smiled as she held up the leaf. 

The fly flew near her, and Sadie realized that she had been playing with the fly for a long time now. She smiled and said goodbye to the fly, then set out on the way back home. As she went, Sadie still held onto the bitter green and yellow leaf.

The worm replied, "Yes, I am slow. But that's how I move." 

Lily watched the worm for a while and said, "I admire your determination to keep moving even though you are slow." 

The worm smiled and said, "Thank you, Lily. I may be slow, but I still have places to go." 

Lily and the worm became friends and would often talk to each other when she played in the garden. From that day on, Lily admired the worm's slow but steady pace.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to surf in the big blue ocean. He would ride the waves and feel so happy. One day, Timmy saw a big sack floating in the water. He thought it was crazy to see a sack in the ocean, but he wanted to see what was inside.

Timmy paddled over to the sack and opened it up. Inside, he found a bunch of shiny things that sparkled in the sun. Timmy was so excited and started to collect all the shiny things. But as he was collecting, he didn't notice the dark clouds rolling in.

Suddenly, a big wave came and knocked Timmy off his surfboard. He tried to swim back up, but the shiny things in the sack were too heavy. Timmy sank down and couldn't breathe anymore. The shiny things were not worth his life. The end.

Once upon a time there was a humble man named Peter. He liked to wander around. One day, he found a strange ashtray in the middle of the street. He picked it up, wondering who left it there.

Meanwhile, not far away, a 3 year old was looking for something. She asked her mum, "Mummy, have you seen my ashtray?"

Mummy replied, "No sweetie, I'm sorry I haven't seen it. Where did you last have it?"

The little girl thought for a moment and then said, "I left it near the shop. I think Peter may have taken it!"

Peter, walking away, was shocked at being accused. He quickly turned around and shouted, "No, I did not take your ashtray!"

The little girl sadly looked away and said, "Well, it's gone now." But Peter began to realise that the ashtray belonged to the little girl. He walked towards her and said, "I'm sorry, here is your ashtray."

The little girl was delighted, "Thank you Peter, you saved me a lot of worry!"

Peter smiled and said, "You're welcome. I should always be humble and not wander off with something that isn't mine."

The little girl nodded in agreement, and they both went their separate ways.

But Max does not like to be wrapped. He feels hot and itchy. He tries to shake off the paper and ribbons. He growls and barks. He runs around the garage and makes a mess.

Lily and Tom hear Lily's mom coming. They are scared. They try to hide behind the box. But Lily's mom sees them and Max. She is not happy. She says, "What have you done to Max? He looks like a giant present! This is not nice. You have to unwrap him and clean up the garage. Now!"

Lily and Tom feel sorry. They say, "We are sorry, mom. We wanted to make you laugh. We love Max. We will unwrap him and clean up. We promise."

They unwrap Max and hug him. He licks their faces. He is glad to be free. They clean up the garage and put the paper and ribbons back in the box. They say, "We will not wrap Max again. We will play with him in the yard. He is a good dog. We are sorry, mom."

Lily's mom smiles and says, "It's okay. I know you meant well. But next time, please ask me before you use my things. And remember, Max is not a toy. He is a living being. He needs love and care. Not paper and ribbons."

Lily and Tom nod and say, "We understand, mom. We love you and Max. Can we go play with him in the yard?"

Lily's mom says, "Yes, you can. But be careful and gentle. And have fun."

Lily and Tom say, "Thank you, mom. We will." They take Max to the yard and play with him. He is happy and alert. He runs and barks. He is a good dog. And Lily and Tom are good friends. The end.

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a big box with many toys. They have cars, balls, dolls, and flags.

One day, they find a new flag in the box. It is red and white and blue. It is very thick and soft. Tim likes the flag. He says, "This is my flag. I own it. It is the best flag ever."

Sam does not agree. He says, "No, this is not your flag. You do not own it. It is our flag. We share it. It is a nice flag, but not the best."

Tim and Sam start to argue. They pull the flag from each other. They shout and cry. They do not want to share the flag. They do not want to be friends.

A lady sees them. She is their teacher. She comes to them and says, "What is wrong, Tim and Sam? Why are you fighting? Why are you not playing nicely?"

Tim and Sam tell her about the flag. They say they both want it. They say they do not want to share it. They say they do not want to be friends.

The lady is sad. She says, "Tim and Sam, you are both wrong. This is not your flag. You do not own it. This is the flag of our country. It is a special flag. It is a symbol of our freedom and unity. It is a flag for everyone. You should respect it and love it. You should not fight over it. You should share it and be proud of it. You should also be friends. Friends do not fight. Friends help each other and have fun together. Do you understand?"

Tim and Sam feel sorry. They say, "Yes, we understand. We are sorry. We did not know. We will not fight over the flag. We will share it and be proud of it. We will also be friends. We will help each other and have fun together."

The lady smiles. She says, "That is good. I am glad. Now, let us go and play with the flag. Let us wave it and sing a song. Let us celebrate our country and our friendship."

Tim and Sam nod. They hold the flag together. They wave it and sing a song. They celebrate their country and their friendship. They are happy. They are friends.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big hill near their house. They wanted to climb it and see what was on the other side.

"Let's go, Lily!" Ben said. "It will be fun!"

"OK, Ben!" Lily said. "But we have to be careful. The hill is steep and rocky."

They held hands and started to walk up the hill. They saw some flowers, some bugs, and some birds. They also saw some clouds in the sky. They were white and fluffy.

"Look, Lily!" Ben said. "The clouds are like animals. That one is like a dog. And that one is like a fish."

"Wow, Ben!" Lily said. "You are right. They are like animals. And they are moving. Where are they going?"

"They are going to the other side of the sky," Ben said. "They are following the sun. The sun is bright and warm. It makes everything clear."

They reached the top of the hill. They looked around and saw the other side. They saw some houses, some trees, and some cars. They also saw some people and some animals.

"Look, Ben!" Lily said. "The other side is like our side. But it is different. The houses are different. The trees are different. The cars are different."

"Wow, Lily!" Ben said. "You are right. The other side is like our side. But it is different. The people are different. The animals are different."

They waved to the people and the animals. Some of them waved back. Some of them smiled. Some of them barked or meowed.

"Hello, other side!" Ben said. "We are Lily and Ben. We are from this side. We climbed the hill to see you."

"Hello, Lily and Ben!" a voice said. "We are Sam and Mia. We are from the other side. We are glad to see you."

Lily and Ben looked and saw two children who were also twins. They had different hair and eyes, but they had the same smile.

"Can we play with you?" Lily asked.

"Of course!" Sam said. "We have a ball and a kite. Do you want to try them?"

"Yes, please!" Ben said.

They ran down the hill and played with Sam and Mia. They had a lot of fun. They learned new games and new words. They shared their snacks and their stories.

They became friends.

The moral of the story is: You can find friends on the other side of the hill, if you are brave and curious. The other side may be different, but it is also like your side. The sun and the clouds are the same for everyone. They make everything clear.

Jenny and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a big bird in a tree. The bird had a wire around its wing. It could not fly. It was sad.

"Look, Tom, a bird!" Jenny said. "It is pretty. It has red and blue feathers. But it is stuck. We have to help it."

"How can we help it, Jenny?" Tom asked. "The tree is too high. We are too small."

Jenny thought hard. She saw a ladder near the fence. She had an idea.

"Tom, get the ladder. I have a plan. We can rescue the bird."

Tom ran to the fence. He dragged the ladder to the tree. He was strong. Jenny climbed the ladder. She was brave. She reached the bird. She spoke softly.

"Hello, bird. Don't be scared. I am here to help you. I will take the wire off your wing. Then you can fly again."

The bird looked at Jenny. It trusted her. Jenny gently untangled the wire from the bird's wing. She threw the wire away. The bird flapped its wing. It was free.

"Thank you, Jenny. You are kind. You are my friend." The bird said.

"You are welcome, bird. You are beautiful. You are my friend too." Jenny said.

The bird flew away. It sang a happy song. Jenny and Tom smiled. They were proud. They had rescued the bird. They hugged each other. They went back to play.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the park with her mom. She saw a big slide and wanted to go on it. She ran to the slide and climbed up the ladder. But when she got to the top, she saw an unknown boy sitting on the slide. He had a big hat and a long coat. He looked at Lily and said, "This is my slide. You can't go on it."

Lily felt scared and sad. She wanted to go on the slide, but the boy was mean. She did not know what to do. She looked at her mom, who was sitting on a bench. She called out, "Mom, mom, help me!"

Her mom heard her and came to the slide. She saw the unknown boy and said, "Hello, what is your name?"

The boy did not answer. He just glared at Lily and her mom.

Her mom said, "Lily, this is a public slide. Everyone can go on it. You can ask the boy to share with you. Can you say, 'Please, can I go on the slide with you?'"

Lily nodded. She felt a little brave. She looked at the boy and said, "Please, can I go on the slide with you?"

The boy did not say anything. He just moved his ear and shook his head.

Her mom said, "That's not very nice. You should share with others. How would you feel if someone did not let you go on the slide?"

The boy did not answer. He just hugged his coat and looked away.

Her mom said, "Lily, I'm sorry, but this boy does not want to share. Maybe we can find another slide or another toy to play with. Come on, let's go."

Lily felt sad, but she agreed. She followed her mom and left the slide. She hoped the unknown boy would learn to share and be kind. She also hoped to find a friend who would play with her on the slide.

Ben and Lily liked to play in the park. They liked to slide, swing and run. One day, they saw a big ship on the water. The ship was tall and had many windows. It looked like a castle.

"Wow, look at the ship!" Ben said. "I want to go on it."

They ran to the edge of the park, where they could see the ship better. They saw some people on the ship. They waved at them.

One of the people heard them and smiled. He was wearing a hat and a coat. He looked like a captain.

"Hello, little ones," he said. "Do you like our ship?"

"Yes, we do," Lily said. "It's very pretty."

"Thank you," the captain said. "It's our home. We travel around the world on it."

"Wow, that's amazing," Ben said. "Can you take us with you?"

The captain laughed. "I'm sorry, but you can't. You have to stay with your parents. They would miss you very much."

Ben and Lily felt sad. They wanted to see the world on the ship.

"Please, captain, please," Ben begged. "Just for a little while."

The captain shook his head. "No, no, it's too dangerous. The ship is not a toy. It has many rules and risks. You could get hurt or lost."

Ben and Lily looked at each other. They had an idea.

"Okay, captain," Lily said. "We understand. But can you promise us something?"

"What is it?" the captain asked.

"Can you promise us that you will come back to the park someday and tell us stories about your travels?" Lily said.

The captain smiled. He liked the children. They were curious and brave.

"Of course, I can promise you that," he said. "I will come back and tell you all about the places I've seen and the people I've met. How does that sound?"

Ben and Lily clapped their hands. They were happy.

"That sounds great," Ben said. "Thank you, captain."

"You're welcome, little ones," the captain said. "Now, go back to your parents. They must be looking for you. And remember, I will keep my promise."

"Wait for me, Ben! I have to deliver these flowers to the hospital!" Lily said, following him with her van. "They will make the sick people happy!"

But no one answered. Ben knocked again, louder. "Hello, is anyone there? I have apples for you!"

Still no answer. Ben felt impatient. He wanted to deliver his apples and get a sticker for being a good driver. He looked at Lily, who was waiting with her van. "Maybe they are not home," he said. "Maybe they went out."

Lily shook her head. "No, they are home. I can hear them. Listen!" She pointed to her ear.

Ben listened. He heard some noises from behind the door. He heard a voice saying, "Shh, be quiet. They are sleeping."

Ben and Lily looked at each other. They realized that the market and the hospital were really their parents' bedroom, and that their parents were taking a nap. They felt sorry for waking them up. They decided to be quiet and deliver their things later.

They waited until their parents woke up and then they delivered their apples and flowers. Their parents were happy and gave them stickers and hugs. Ben and Lily were happy too. They learned to be patient and respectful.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big truck coming on the road. The truck was loud and fast.

"Look, a truck!" Tom said.

"Let's go see!" Lily said.

They ran to the fence. They wanted to touch the truck. But the truck did not stop. It did not yield. It went on and on.

"Stop, truck, stop!" Tom and Lily shouted.

But the truck did not hear them. It did not care. It was too busy.

The truck passed by a fire hydrant. The fire hydrant was old and weak. It could not hold the water. The water burst out of the fire hydrant. It was hot and strong. It sprayed the truck and the fence and the park.

"Wow, water!" Tom said.

"Let's go play!" Lily said.

They ran to the water. They wanted to feel the water. But the water was too hot. It burned their skin. It hurt their eyes.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom and Lily cried.

They ran away from the water. They looked for help. They saw a man with a hat and a hose. He was a fireman. He came to the park. He wanted to stop the water.

"Are you okay, kids?" the fireman asked.

"No, we are not okay!" Tom and Lily said.

"The water is hot and bad!"

The fireman nodded. He used his hose. He sprayed the water with his hose. His hose had cold and light water. It was good and nice. It cooled the hot water. It made the hot water stop.

"Thank you, fireman!" Tom and Lily said.

"You're welcome, kids!" the fireman said.

"But you should be careful. You should not run to the road. You should not touch the truck. You should yield to the truck. The truck is big and dangerous. It can hurt you."

Tom and Lily nodded. They learned their lesson. They said sorry to the fireman. They hugged the fireman. They went back to their play. They did not run to the road. They did not touch the truck. They yielded to the truck. They were safe and happy.

Tom is a big boy who likes to cook. He has a uniform with a hat and an apron. He helps his mom in the kitchen every day. He can stir, pour, and taste. He is very good at cooking.

One day, Tom wants to make a cake for his dad. He asks his mom, "Can I cook a cake for dad? He will be happy."

His mom says, "Yes, you can. But you need to follow the recipe and be careful. Cooking is fun, but it can also be hot and messy."

Tom says, "OK, mom. I will follow the recipe and be careful. I will make the best cake ever."

Tom puts on his uniform and gets the ingredients. He mixes the flour, the sugar, the eggs, and the milk in a big bowl. He adds some chocolate chips and some vanilla. He stirs and stirs until the batter is smooth. He pours the batter into a cake pan and puts it in the oven. He sets the timer and waits.

He smells the cake baking. It smells yummy. He is excited to see the cake. He hopes his dad will like it. He cleans the bowl and the spoon. He is a good helper.

When the timer rings, he takes the cake out of the oven. He lets it cool down. He puts some frosting and some sprinkles on top. He writes "I love you, dad" with a red icing. He is proud of his cake.

He shows his mom his cake. She says, "Wow, Tom, you did a great job. Your cake looks delicious and beautiful. I'm sure your dad will love it. You are a wonderful cook."

Tom smiles and hugs his mom. He says, "Thank you, mom. You are a wonderful cook, too. Can we surprise dad with the cake?"

His mom says, "Yes, we can. Let's put the cake on a plate and hide it under a cloth. When dad comes home, we will say 'Surprise!' and give him the cake."

Tom says, "OK, mom. That sounds fun. I can't wait to see dad's face."

They put the cake on a plate and hide it under a cloth. They wait for dad to come home. They are happy and excited. They love to cook and they love their dad.

One day, they go on the subway to visit Grandma. Mom says, "We get off at the fifth stop. Can you repeat that?" Tom and Lily say, "Fifth stop, fifth stop." Mom smiles and says, "Good job."

Mom runs to a man in a uniform. She says, "Help, help! My twins are on the subway!" The man says, "Don't worry, we will find them. What do they look like?" Mom says, "They have red hair and blue eyes. They are wearing yellow shirts and green pants. They are four years old." The man says, "OK, I will call the next station. They will stop the subway and wait for you. Come with me."

Tom and Lily see the man on the phone. They hear him say their names. They say, "That's us, that's us!" They wave and shout. The man sees them and says, "There they are! Are you OK?" Tom and Lily say, "Yes, we are OK. But where is Mom?" The man says, "She is coming. She is very worried. You should have listened to her and repeated what she said. That is important." Tom and Lily say, "We are sorry. We will listen and repeat next time." The man says, "Good. Now, let's go and meet Mom. She will be very happy to see you."

Lily was so happy. She climbed on the chair with her dad's help and sat on it. "Wow, this chair is very comfortable!" she said. Her dad smiled and said, "Yes, it's an attractive chair, isn't it?" Lily nodded and said, "I love it!"

Lila and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big flower. It is yellow and red. It smells good.

"Wow, look at the flower!" Tom says. "It is so pretty!"

"Yes, it is," Lila agrees. "Can we pick it?"

Tom shakes his head. "No, we can't. Mom says we should not pick flowers. They are alive. They need water and sun."

Lila nods. "You are right. Mom says that too. But can we touch it?"

Tom thinks. "Maybe we can. But we have to be gentle. We don't want to hurt the flower."

They go closer to the flower. They touch it softly. The petals are smooth and soft. The stem is green and strong.

"Listen," Lila says. "Do you hear that?"

Tom listens. He hears a buzzing sound. He sees a bee. The bee is flying around the flower. It is looking for nectar.

"Look, a bee!" Tom says. "It likes the flower too!"

"Yes, it does," Lila says. "The bee is graceful. It can fly and land on the flower. It can make honey."

They watch the bee for a while. They see how it moves from one flower to another. They smile. They are happy. They like the flower and the bee. They are friends.
