Tom and Lily were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a man with a big whip and a red hat. He was making loud noises and cracking his whip at some animals. Tom and Lily were scared and worried. They hid behind a tree and watched.

"Who is he?" Lily whispered.

"I don't know. Maybe he is a bad man. He is hurting the animals," Tom said.

"Why does he do that?" Lily asked.

"Maybe he wants to make them do tricks. But that is not nice. The animals are scared too," Tom said.

They saw the man whip a lion, a bear, and a monkey. The animals roared, growled, and screeched. Tom and Lily felt sorry for them. They wanted to help, but they did not know how.

Then, they saw a boy with a basket. He was selling hot dogs and drinks to the people who came to watch the man and the animals. Tom had an idea.

"Look, Lily. He has spicy sauce. Maybe we can use it to stop the bad man," Tom said.

"How?" Lily asked.

"Follow me," Tom said.

They ran to the boy and asked for two hot dogs with spicy sauce. The boy gave them the hot dogs and took their money. Tom and Lily thanked him and ran back to the tree. They waited for the right moment.

When the man was about to whip the lion again, Tom threw his hot dog at him. The hot dog hit the man's face and the spicy sauce went into his eyes and mouth. The man screamed and dropped his whip. He rubbed his eyes and spat out the sauce. He was very angry.

"Who did that? Who threw that hot dog at me?" he shouted.

Lily threw her hot dog at him too. The hot dog hit his red hat and knocked it off. The man was even more angry.

"Who did that? Who threw that hot dog at me?" he shouted again.

Tom and Lily ran out from behind the tree. They shouted at the man.

"Stop hurting the animals! They are not your toys! They have feelings too!" they said.

The people who came to watch the man and the animals saw what Tom and Lily did. They clapped and cheered for them. They booed and jeered at the man. They told him to leave the park and never come back. The man was ashamed and afraid. He ran away with his whip and his hat.

The animals were happy and grateful. They licked and hugged Tom and Lily. They thanked them for saving them. Tom and Lily smiled and petted them. They made new friends.

The moral of the story is: Be kind to animals. They are not for hurting. They are for loving.

One night, she wanted to show her glow string to her friend Ben. He came to her house for a sleepover. They ate pizza and watched a funny movie. Then they went to Sara's room and turned off the lamp. Sara took out her glow string and said, "Look, Ben, I can make a star!"

She waved her glow string in the air and made a star. Ben said, "Wow, that's cool! Can I try?" Sara said, "Sure, here you go." She gave him her glow string and he tried to make a star too. But it was difficult. He could not make the points of the star. His star looked like a blob.

Sara said, "Don't worry, Ben, it's hard to make a star. You have to move your hand fast and stop at the right time. Do you want me to help you?" Ben said, "Yes, please." Sara said, "OK, let's do it together. Hold one end of the glow string and I'll hold the other. Now, follow me."

They moved their hands together and made a star. Ben said, "Yay, we did it! Thank you, Sara, you're a good friend." Sara said, "You're welcome, Ben, you're a good friend too. Do you want to make another shape?" Ben said, "Yes, let's make a heart!" They made a heart and then an S and then a B. They had fun with the glow string until they fell asleep.

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big tree with many pears on it. They wanted to pick some pears, but the tree was too high for them.

"Let's ask Dad to help us," Tom said.

"No, we can do it by ourselves," Sam said. "We are mighty boys. We don't need Dad."

Sam found a big stick and tried to hit the pears with it. But he missed and hit Tom on the head.

"Ow! That hurts!" Tom cried.

"Sorry, sorry," Sam said. "Let me try again."

Sam swung the stick again, but this time he hit a bee's nest. The bees came out and buzzed around them.

"Run, run!" Tom shouted.

They ran away from the tree, but the bees followed them. They ran to their house and slammed the door.

"Dad, Dad, help us!" they cried.

Dad came and saw the bees outside. He opened the window and shooed them away.

"What happened, boys?" he asked.

"We wanted to pick some pears, but we made the bees angry," Tom said.

"Why didn't you ask me to help you?" Dad asked.

Sam shrugged. He didn't know what to say.

Dad hugged them and said, "It's okay, boys. I'm glad you are safe. But next time, remember to ask for help when you need it. You are mighty, but you are not alone. You have me and Tom and Mom. We are a team. We can do things better together."

Tom and Sam nodded. They learned their lesson. They said sorry to each other and to Dad. Then they went to the kitchen and ate some pears that Dad had bought for them. They were sweet and juicy. They smiled and thanked Dad. They were happy.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they decided to go to the valley near their house. The valley had a big river and many trees and flowers. Anna and Ben loved to look at the water and the animals.

"Let's go to the bridge and throw stones in the river," Ben said.

"Okay, but we have to be careful. The bridge is old and wet. Mommy told us not to go too close to the edge," Anna said.

Ben nodded, but he was not really listening. He wanted to see how far he could throw his stones. He ran ahead of Anna and climbed on the bridge. He found a big stone and threw it with all his might. The stone made a big splash in the river.

"Wow, did you see that?" Ben shouted.

Anna caught up with him and saw him standing on the edge of the bridge. She felt scared.

"Ben, come back. The bridge is not safe. You could fall in the water," Anna said.

Ben did not listen. He found another stone and threw it again. He leaned over the edge to see the splash. But he leaned too far. He lost his balance and slipped. He screamed as he fell in the river.

"Ben!" Anna cried.

She ran to the other side of the bridge and looked for Ben. She saw him floating in the water. He was wet and cold and scared. He tried to swim, but the water was too fast and deep. He called for help.

"Anna, help me!"

Anna did not know what to do. She remembered what Mommy had told them. She had given them a whistle and said, "If you ever need help, blow this whistle and someone will come."

Anna took out the whistle and blew it as hard as she could. She hoped someone would hear it and come to save Ben.

Soon, she heard a siren. It was a fire truck. The firemen had heard the whistle and followed the sound. They saw Anna on the bridge and Ben in the river. They quickly got a rope and threw it to Ben. Ben grabbed the rope and the firemen pulled him out of the water. They wrapped him in a blanket and put him in the truck.

"Are you okay, Ben?" Anna asked.

Ben nodded, but he was shivering and crying. He was sorry for not listening to Anna and Mommy. He had learned a hard lesson.

The firemen drove them back to their house. Mommy was waiting for them. She was worried and angry. She hugged them and scolded them.

"Why did you go to the bridge? Why did you not listen to me? You could have drowned, Ben. You were very foolish and reckless," Mommy said.

"I'm sorry, Mommy. I'm sorry, Anna. I won't do it again. I promise," Ben said.

Mommy forgave them, but she made them stay inside for the rest of the day. She reminded them to be careful and obey the rules. She said, "The rules are there to protect you, not to spoil your fun. You have to respect the rules and each other. You have to be responsible and smart. You have to be thankful for your life and your sister."

Anna and Ben nodded. They understood. They hugged each other and said, "We love you, Mommy. We love you, sister. We love you, brother."

The end.

Lily was a busy girl. She liked to play with her toys, draw with her crayons, and read her books. She had a lot of fun in her room, but sometimes she wanted more space.

One day, she asked her mom if she could go outside and play. Her mom said yes, but she had to wear her coat and hat. It was cold and windy outside. Lily put on her warm clothes and ran to the door.

She saw a big pile of leaves in the yard. She wanted to jump in them and make them fly. She ran to the pile and jumped with a big smile. She felt the leaves crunch under her feet and tickle her nose.

But then, she felt a tickle in her nose that was not from the leaves. She felt a sneeze coming. She tried to stop it, but it was too strong. She sneezed so hard that she blew all the leaves away. She sneezed again and again, and the leaves flew in the air.

She looked around and saw that she had made a big mess. The leaves were everywhere, on the grass, on the fence, on the roof. She felt sorry for making such a mess. She wanted to clean it up, but she did not know how.

She heard her mom call her name. She ran to the door and saw her mom holding a tissue. Her mom smiled and said, "Bless you, Lily. You have a big sneeze. Come inside and have some soup. You need to rest."

Lily nodded and followed her mom. She was glad that her mom was not mad at her. She hoped that her sneeze would go away soon. She wanted to play outside again, but with more space and less leaves.

"No, it hurts a lot!" Ben said, with tears in his eyes.

Sara thought for a moment. She remembered that her mom had a band-aid in her bag. She ran to the bench where her mom was sitting and reading a book.

"Mom, mom, Ben needs a band-aid!" she said, pointing to Ben.

Her mom looked up and saw Ben on the ground. She quickly got up and took a band-aid from her bag.

"Thank you, Sara, you are very helpful!" she said, as she walked to Ben.

She cleaned his wound and put the band-aid on it.

"There, all better!" she said, with a smile.

Ben smiled too. He felt better now.

"Thank you, mom, thank you, Sara!" he said, hugging them.

Sara hugged him back.

"You're welcome, Ben. I'm glad you're okay. Do you want to play some more?" she asked.

Ben nodded.

"Yes, but not too high!" he said.

They laughed and ran to the slide. They had fun in the park. It was spring, and they were happy.

Anna and Ben were friends who liked to play outside. They saw a big tree with many green leaves and red fruits. They wanted to touch the fruits and see how they tasted.

"Look, Ben, the fruits are so pretty and shiny. Let's go and touch them," Anna said.

"OK, Anna, but be careful. Maybe they are not good for us," Ben said.

They ran to the tree and reached for the fruits. But as soon as they touched them, they felt a sharp pain in their fingers. The fruits were not fruits, but spiky balls that hurt a lot.

"Ow, ow, ow! Anna, it hurts! Let go of the fruit!" Ben cried.

"Ow, ow, ow! Ben, I can't! The fruit is stuck to my hand!" Anna cried.

They tried to pull their hands away, but the spiky balls were too strong. They started to bleed and cry louder and louder.

A man who was walking by heard their cries and came to help them. He saw the tree and the spiky balls and shook his head.

"You silly children, why did you touch the tree? Don't you know that this is a cactus? It has needles that can hurt you very much. You are not intelligent at all," he said.

He took out a knife and cut the spiky balls from their hands. He wrapped their hands with a cloth and took them to a doctor. The doctor gave them some medicine and a bandage and told them to be more careful next time.

Anna and Ben learned a hard lesson that day. They never touched the cactus tree again. They were sad and ashamed and wished they had been more intelligent.

Timmy said, "Don't worry, I can play my trumpet for you. It will make you feel better." So, Timmy played his trumpet for the man. The man smiled and said, "Thank you, that was beautiful. You speak with your music." From that day on, Timmy would visit the man every week and play his trumpet for him. They became good friends and Timmy learned that sometimes the best way to help someone is to speak with your heart, not just your words.

Timmy felt bad for the man and wished he could make him feel better. He decided to draw a picture of the yacht and give it to the man as a present. The man smiled and thanked Timmy. From that day on, Timmy learned that even small acts of kindness can make someone's day better.

One day, a little ant was walking on a leaf. He saw a big spider on another leaf. The spider looked hungry and scary.

"Hello, spider," the ant said. "Do you want to hear a joke?"

The spider was surprised. He did not like jokes. He liked to eat ants.

"A joke? What is a joke?" the spider asked.

"A joke is something funny that makes you laugh," the ant said. "I know a very funny joke. Do you want to hear it?"

The spider thought for a moment. He was curious. Maybe the joke was so funny that he would forget about his hunger.

"Okay, tell me your joke," the spider said.

The ant smiled. He had a clever plan. He said, "Why did the chicken cross the road?"

The spider waited. He did not know what a chicken was, or what a road was.

"I don't know. Why?" the spider asked.

The ant said, "To get to the other side!"

The spider did not understand. He did not laugh. He was angry.

"That is not a joke. That is nonsense. You are wasting my time. Now I will eat you!" the spider said.

He jumped from his leaf to the ant's leaf. But the ant was ready. He quickly ran to the edge of the leaf and jumped to another leaf. The spider missed him and fell to the ground.

"Ha ha ha! That was my joke. To get to the other side of the leaf. You are not clever, spider. You are silly. Goodbye!" the ant said.

He ran away and found his friends. He told them his joke and they all laughed. They were happy and safe.

The moral of the story is: Sometimes, a joke can save your life. You have to be clever and brave. And you have to know when to run.

Her mother always told her to stay close to the river, where it was safe from the hunters. The hunters were bad men who wanted to hurt the animals with their loud sticks.

One day, Lila saw a bright flower on the other side of the forest. She wanted to smell it and touch it, so she ran away from the river. She did not tell her friends or her mother where she was going. She forgot what her mother said about the hunters.

She reached the flower and bent down to sniff it. It smelled very sweet and pretty. She smiled and picked it up. She did not see the hunter hiding behind a tree. He saw Lila and aimed his loud stick at her. He was about to shoot when he heard a voice.

"Lila, where are you?" It was her mother, looking for her. She heard the loud stick and ran towards the sound. She saw the hunter and the flower and Lila. She was very scared and angry. She shouted at the hunter, "Leave my baby alone!"

The hunter was surprised and scared too. He did not want to fight with a big deer. He dropped his loud stick and ran away. Lila's mother ran to her and hugged her. She was very happy that she was not hurt. She said, "Lila, I'm so glad you're safe. But why did you run away from the river? Why did you forget what I told you?"

Her mother said, "I forgive you, Lila. But you have to promise me that you will never do that again. The hunters are very dangerous and they can hurt you. You have to listen to me and stay close to the river. That's where you belong. That's where you are safe."

Lila nodded and said, "I promise, mother. I will listen to you and stay close to the river. I don't want to see the hunters ever again. I love you, mother."

Her mother said, "I love you too, Lila. Come on, let's go back to the river and find your friends. They must be worried about you."

"Can we go closer to the hippo, mom?" Lily asked.

"Sure, but be careful. The hippo is very strong and can bite," mom said.

Lily and Ben walked to the fence that separated them from the hippo. They saw the hippo open its mouth and show its big teeth. It made a loud noise, like a snort.

"Wow, look at its teeth!" Ben said.

"I want to touch it," Lily said.

She saw a small hill near the fence. She had an idea. She ran to the hill and started to climb it. She wanted to reach the top and see the hippo better.

"Wait, Lily, don't do that!" Ben shouted.

But Lily did not listen. She climbed higher and higher, until she was almost at the top. She felt warm and happy. She was about to see the hippo up close.

But then, something bad happened. The hill was not a hill. It was the hippo's back. The hippo felt Lily's feet on its skin. It did not like it. It turned around and saw Lily on its back. It was angry. It shook its head and tried to throw Lily off.

Lily was scared. She screamed and held on to the hippo's back. She wished she had listened to Ben and mom. She wanted to get off the hippo and run away.

"Help, help!" she cried.

Mom and Ben heard Lily's scream. They saw her on the hippo's back. They were scared too. They ran to the fence and called for help.

"Someone, help! There's a girl on the hippo's back!" mom shouted.

A zookeeper heard mom's shout. He saw Lily on the hippo's back. He ran to the fence with a big stick. He used the stick to poke the hippo and make it stop moving. He talked to the hippo in a calm voice.

"Easy, easy, boy. It's okay. It's just a little girl. She didn't mean to bother you. Let her go, please," he said.

The hippo heard the zookeeper's voice. It recognized him. He was the one who fed it and gave it water. It trusted him. It stopped shaking its head and calmed down. It let Lily slide off its back and onto the ground.

Lily was safe. She was dirty and wet, but not hurt. She ran to mom and Ben and hugged them. She was sorry and scared.

Mom and Ben hugged her back. They were glad she was okay. They thanked the zookeeper for saving her.

"It's okay, Lily. We're happy you're fine. But don't ever climb on a hippo again. It's very dangerous. Hippos are not for climbing. They are for watching and learning," mom said.

Lily nodded. She learned her lesson. She looked at the hippo and said sorry.

"Sorry, hippo. You're very big and strong. I won't climb on you again. I hope you're not mad at me," she said.

Lily and Ben were very sorry. They knew they did something wrong. They wished they had told someone about their plan. They wished they had not used an alarm. They wished they had not scared everyone.

The moral of the story is: Always tell someone about your plans. Do not use things that can be dangerous. Do not scare people for no reason. Be responsible and respectful.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play together. But they did not like to wash their hands or faces. They thought it was boring and hard. They wanted to be lazy and have fun.

One day, their mom said, "Ben and Lily, you have to wash up. We are going to visit your aunt at the university. She is a teacher there and she will show you her classroom and her books."

Ben and Lily groaned. They did not want to go to the university. They wanted to stay home and play with their toys. They did not want to see their aunt or her books. They thought they were too big for that.

They tried to hide under the bed, but their mom found them. She said, "Come on, you two. You have to wash up. It is not nice to be dirty and smelly. Your aunt will be sad if you don't come. She has a surprise for you."

Ben and Lily wondered what the surprise was. They hoped it was something good, like candy or a toy. They decided to wash up, but they did it very quickly and carelessly. They did not use soap or water. They just rubbed their hands and faces with a dry towel.

They got in the car with their mom and drove to the university. They saw a big building with many windows and doors. They saw many people walking and talking. They saw their aunt waving at them. She looked happy and smart.

She hugged them and said, "Hello, Ben and Lily. I'm so glad you came. I have a surprise for you. Do you want to see it?"

Ben and Lily nodded. They followed their aunt to her classroom. She opened the door and said, "Look, this is my surprise. I have a pet in my classroom. His name is Fluffy and he is a rabbit. He is very soft and cute. Do you want to pet him?"

Ben and Lily gasped. They loved animals. They ran to the cage where Fluffy was. They reached out their hands to touch him. But Fluffy did not like their hands. He smelled them and made a loud noise. He bit their fingers and scratched their palms. He was very angry and scared.

Ben and Lily cried. They pulled back their hands and looked at them. They were red and sore. They wondered why Fluffy did that. They looked at their aunt. She looked sad and sorry.

She said, "Oh, Ben and Lily, I'm so sorry. Fluffy is not used to dirty hands. He likes clean hands. He thinks dirty hands are bad and mean. He was trying to protect himself. You have to wash your hands with soap and water before you pet him. Then he will be nice and friendly."

Ben and Lily realized their mistake. They felt bad and ashamed. They said, "We're sorry, auntie. We did not wash our hands well. We were lazy and rude. We will wash our hands now. Can we try again?"

Their aunt smiled and said, "Of course, you can. But you have to be gentle and quiet. Fluffy is a shy and sweet rabbit. He likes to be loved and cared for. Come on, let's go to the bathroom and wash your hands properly. Then we can come back and pet him."

Ben and Lily nodded. They followed their aunt to the bathroom. They washed their hands with soap and water. They dried them with a clean towel. They felt better and happier.

They went back to the classroom. They approached Fluffy slowly and softly. They said, "Hello, Fluffy. We're sorry we scared you. We washed our hands. Can we be your friends?"

Fluffy sniffed their hands and made a soft noise. He licked their fingers and rubbed his nose against their palms. He was very calm and happy.

Ben and Lily smiled. They petted him and stroked his fur. They said, "You are very soft and cute, Fluffy. We like you. You are a good surprise. Thank you, auntie."

Their aunt hugged them and said, "You're welcome, Ben and Lily. I'm proud of you. You learned a good lesson today. Washing your hands is important and respectful. It makes you and others healthy and happy. It is not boring or hard. It is easy and fun."

Ben and Lily agreed. They said, "We will wash our hands every day. We will not be lazy or rude. We will be clean and nice. We will love Fluffy and you."

They spent the rest of the day playing with Fluffy and their aunt. They had a lot of fun and learned a lot of things. They were not bored or sad. They were glad and grateful. They liked the university and their aunt. They liked washing their hands.

"No, Lily, you have to come with me. We need to buy more spaghetti and other things. It won't take long, I promise. You can bring your teddy bear with you, okay?"

Lily was not happy, but she nodded. She put on her coat and shoes and grabbed her teddy bear. She followed her mom to the car. She hoped they would come back soon.

At the store, Lily's mom put her in a cart and pushed her around. Lily saw many things, but she did not care. She only wanted spaghetti. She held her teddy bear tight and looked around. She saw a big sign that said "Spaghetti". She pointed to it and said, "Mom, look! Spaghetti!"

"Yes, Lily, I see it. We're going to get some, don't worry. But first, we need to get some milk and eggs and bread. Can you help me find them?"

Lily tried to help, but she was bored. She wanted to go home and eat spaghetti. She wished she could stay and play with her teddy bear. She did not notice when her mom turned the corner and left her alone in the cart. She did not notice when a man came and took her teddy bear from her arms. She did not notice until she heard a voice say, "Hey, kid, this is mine now."

Lily looked up and saw a mean man holding her teddy bear. He had a big nose and a dirty beard and a scary smile. He laughed and ran away with her teddy bear. Lily was shocked and scared. She screamed, "No! Give me back my teddy bear! Mom! Mom!"

Lily's mom heard her scream and came running. She saw the man with the teddy bear and chased him. She yelled, "Stop! Thief! Give me back my daughter's teddy bear!"

The man ran faster, but he did not see a banana peel on the floor. He slipped and fell and dropped the teddy bear. Lily's mom caught up and grabbed the teddy bear. She gave it back to Lily and hugged her. She said, "I'm so sorry, Lily. I should have never left you alone. Are you okay?"

Lily nodded and hugged her mom and her teddy bear. She said, "I'm okay, mom. But I was very worried. I thought I lost my teddy bear forever. He loves spaghetti, you know."

Lily's mom smiled and said, "I know, Lily. I love spaghetti too. And I love you more. Come on, let's go home and make some spaghetti. And maybe some cookies too. How does that sound?"

Lily smiled and said, "That sounds great, mom. I love you too. And I love spaghetti. And cookies. And my teddy bear."

They left the store and went home. They made spaghetti and cookies and ate them together. They played with the teddy bear and read a story. They were happy and safe. They never wanted to leave each other again. They always wanted to stay.

Anna liked to visit her grandma every week. Grandma had a big garden with many flowers. Anna's favorite flower was the rose. It was red and smelled nice.

One day, Anna saw a new rose in the garden. It was yellow and shiny. Anna wanted to touch it, but she remembered what grandma said. "Be careful, roses have thorns. They can hurt you if you touch them." Anna was an obedient girl. She did not touch the rose.

But then, a bee came and landed on the rose. Anna was curious. She wanted to see the bee. She moved closer to the rose. The bee did not like that. It buzzed and flew away. But it also stung Anna's hand. Anna cried out loud. It hurt a lot.

Grandma heard Anna's cry. She ran to the garden. She saw Anna's hand. It was red and swollen. Grandma took Anna inside. She put some ice on her hand. She gave her a hug and a kiss. She said, "I'm sorry, Anna. Bees can sting you if you bother them. Next time, be more careful. I love you." Anna said, "I love you too, grandma. I'm sorry I was not obedient." Grandma smiled and said, "It's okay, Anna. You are a good girl. Now, let's have some cookies and milk." Anna smiled too. She felt better. She still liked roses, but she learned to respect them.

Tim and Lily were twins who liked to eat toast for breakfast. They had a big toaster that made four slices of toast at a time. But Tim and Lily always wanted the same slice of toast, the one that was the most golden and crispy. They would fight over it and pull it from each other's hands.

One morning, their mom saw them fighting and said, "Stop it, you two! You should share and be humble. There are other slices of toast that are just as good. And there are other children who have no toast at all. How would you feel if you had nothing to eat?"

Tim and Lily felt ashamed and sorry. They looked at each other and said, "We're sorry, mom. We're sorry, brother/sister. We don't want to be greedy and mean. We want to be kind and grateful."

They decided to release the slice of toast they were fighting over and give it to their mom. They said, "Here, mom. You can have this slice of toast. You work hard and you deserve it. We love you."

Their mom smiled and hugged them. She said, "Thank you, my sweet children. You have made me very happy. You have learned a valuable lesson today. It is better to give than to receive. And it is better to be humble than to be proud."

She cut the slice of toast in half and gave each of them a piece. They ate it happily and thanked their mom. They also thanked God for giving them toast and a loving family. They learned to appreciate what they had and to share with others. They were humble and happy.

"Let's go and see," said Tim. He was brave and curious.

"No, don't go," said Mia. She was frightened and careful. "It might be scary or dangerous."

But Tim did not listen. He climbed over the fence and ran to the house. He opened the door and went in. Mia followed him. She did not want to be alone.

Inside the house, they saw many things. There were chairs, tables, books, pictures and clothes. They were all old and dusty. Tim and Mia touched and moved them. They made a lot of noise.

Suddenly, they heard a loud roar. It came from upstairs. They looked up and saw a big, angry dog. It had sharp teeth and fur. It did not like Tim and Mia. It wanted to destroy them.

"Run!" shouted Tim. He and Mia ran to the door. But the dog was faster. It jumped and bit Tim's leg. Tim cried and fell. Mia screamed and helped him. She threw a book at the dog. The dog let go and barked.

Tim and Mia got out of the house. They climbed over the fence and ran to their garden. They were hurt and scared. They hugged each other and cried.

Their mom heard them and came out. She saw their wounds and dirt. She was shocked and angry.

"What happened?" she asked. "Where did you go?"

Tim and Mia told her about the old house and the dog. They said they were sorry. They learned their lesson.

Mom took them inside. She cleaned and bandaged their wounds. She gave them a hug and a kiss. She said she loved them. She also said they should never go to the old house again. It was not safe or fun.

Tim and Mia agreed. They said they loved her too. They also said they would play with their toys in the garden. They would not be curious or brave. They would be careful and happy.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play in the garden. One day, they found a big green plant with small leaves that smelled nice. They picked some leaves and tasted them. They were mint!

"Mint is yummy!" Tom said. "Let's take some home and make tea."

"Okay!" Lily agreed. "But we should ask Mom first."

They ran to the house and showed Mom the mint. Mom smiled and said they could make tea, but they had to share with Dad and Grandma.

Tom and Lily nodded and went to the kitchen. They boiled some water and put the mint in a pot. Then they poured the tea into four cups.

"Who wants sugar?" Mom asked.

"I do!" Tom said. "I want a lot of sugar. Sugar makes the tea sweet and rich."

"I don't," Lily said. "I like the tea as it is. Mint is sweet enough for me."

Mom gave Tom a spoon and a bowl of sugar. Tom scooped a lot of sugar and put it in his cup. He stirred and tasted it. He made a face.

"Yuck!" he said. "This is too sweet. It hurts my teeth."

Lily giggled and sipped her tea. She smiled.

"Mmm!" she said. "This is perfect. It is fresh and tasty."

Mom looked at Tom and Lily and said, "Sometimes, less is more. You don't need to add too much sugar to enjoy the mint. It is good by itself. You should choose wisely what you put in your tea and in your body."

Tom nodded and poured some of his tea into another cup. He added less sugar and tasted it again. He liked it better.

"Mom is right," he said. "Mint is good by itself. I choose to have less sugar."

Lily hugged Tom and said, "I'm glad you like it. Mint is good for sharing."

They drank their tea and shared it with Dad and Grandma. They all enjoyed the mint and thanked Tom and Lily for finding it. Tom and Lily felt happy and proud. They learned to choose wisely and to appreciate the mint.

Lily was a little girl who liked to go to the park with her mom. She loved to see the birds and the flowers and the pond. One day, she saw a big white bird with a long neck and a curved beak. It was a swan, and it was swimming in the water.

"Mom, look at the swan!" Lily said. "It is so pretty and graceful. Can I touch it?"

Mom shook her head. "No, Lily, you can't touch the swan. It might bite you or flap its wings. It is not a toy, it is a living thing. You have to be gentle and respectful with animals."

Lily nodded, but she was curious. She wanted to see the swan up close. She waited until mom was talking to another mom on the bench. Then she sneaked to the edge of the pond and reached out her hand to the swan.

The swan did not like that. It hissed and snapped at Lily's fingers. Lily screamed and pulled back her hand. It hurt and it was bleeding. Mom heard her cry and ran to her. She saw what happened and hugged Lily.

"I'm sorry, mom, I'm sorry," Lily sobbed. "I just wanted to touch the swan. It was so pretty and graceful."

Mom kissed her hand and wrapped it in a tissue. "I know, Lily, I know. But you have to listen to me when I tell you something. The swan was pretty and graceful, but it was also scared and angry. You scared it and made it angry when you tried to touch it. You have to be careful and kind with animals. They have feelings too, you know."

Lily nodded. She learned her lesson. She looked at the pond and saw the swan swimming away. She felt sorry for the swan and for herself. She wished she could say sorry to the swan.

Then she saw something that made her smile. There was another bird in the pond. It was smaller and rounder and had a short neck and a flat beak. It was a duck, and it was pink. It was the prettiest duck Lily had ever seen.

"Mom, look at the duck!" Lily said. "It is so cute and funny. Can I feed it?"

Mom smiled. She took out some bread crumbs from her bag and gave them to Lily. "Yes, Lily, you can feed the duck. But you have to do it gently and respectfully. You have to throw the bread crumbs into the water, not at the duck. And you have to keep a safe distance, not get too close. The duck might like you, but it might also be shy or nervous. You have to be friendly and polite with animals."

Lily nodded. She did what mom said. She threw the bread crumbs into the water and watched the duck eat them. The duck quacked and wagged its tail. It seemed happy and grateful. Lily felt happy and grateful too. She thanked mom and the duck.

She learned her lesson. She learned that animals are not toys, they are living things. She learned that animals have feelings, and they need to be treated with care and respect. She learned that animals can be pretty and graceful, or cute and funny, or both. She learned that animals can be friends, if you are nice to them.

She learned that being nice is better than being curious.

But the water did not increase. It went out of the tub faster than it came in. The drain was too big. Tim did not know what to do. He looked around for something to stop the drain. He saw a ball. It was an ordinary ball. It was red and round. He thought it might fit in the hole.

He took the ball and pushed it into the drain. It was a tight fit. The water stopped going out of the tub. The tub started to fill up again. Tim was happy. He turned off the hose and played with his toys. He had more water than before. He thanked the ball for saving the day. He said it was not an ordinary ball. It was a special ball. He gave it a hug and a kiss. He put it in the tub with his other toys. They all had fun.

Tom is a bee. He lives in a hive with many other bees. They work hard to make honey and help the flowers. Tom likes his job, but he also likes to have fun.

One day, Tom sees a big truck near the hive. The truck has many boxes with pictures of food on them. Tom is curious. He flies closer to the truck and sees a window. Inside the window, there is a man. The man talks to a box and gets food from another window.

Tom thinks this is amazing. He wants to try it too. He flies to the box and says "buzz buzz buzz". He hopes the man will understand him and give him some food. He waits for a long time, but nothing happens.

Tom is sad. He thinks the man does not like bees. He flies away from the truck and back to the hive. He tells his friends what he saw and what he tried to do. They laugh at him and say he is silly. They say bees do not order food from trucks. They say bees make their own food from flowers.

Tom feels bad. He wishes he could order food from trucks like the man. He thinks the man is lucky. He does not have to work hard to get food. He can just talk to a box and get what he wants.

But then, Tom sees something else. He sees a bear. The bear is big and hungry. The bear smells the honey in the hive. The bear runs to the hive and tries to break it. The bees are scared. They fly out of the hive and sting the bear. The bear roars and runs away.

Tom is happy. He is glad he is a bee. He is glad he lives in a hive with his friends. He is glad he makes honey and helps the flowers. He thinks he is lucky. He does not have to worry about bears. He can just buzz and be happy.

Anna liked to help her mom in the kitchen. She wanted to learn how to cook and make yummy food. One day, her mom gave her a radish to cut. A radish is a red and white vegetable that is crunchy and spicy.

Anna took a big knife and tried to cut the radish. But the knife was too sharp and the radish was too hard. She pushed too hard and the knife slipped. She cut her finger and it hurt a lot. She cried and dropped the knife and the radish.

Her mom heard her cry and ran to her. She saw the blood and the mess and hugged Anna. She said, "Oh, Anna, I'm sorry. You should not use a big knife to cut a radish. A big knife is for grown-ups. A radish is delicate and needs a small knife and a gentle hand. Let me clean your wound and put a band-aid on it. Then I will show you how to cut a radish safely and carefully."

Anna felt better and said sorry to her mom. She said, "I wanted to help you, mom. I wanted to be like you. But I was not careful and I hurt myself and the radish. I will listen to you next time and use a small knife and a gentle hand."

Her mom smiled and said, "I love you, Anna. You are a good helper and a good learner. But you also need to be patient and cautious. Cutting a radish is not easy. It takes skill and practice. You will learn how to do it when you are older and stronger. For now, you can help me with other things, like washing the dishes or stirring the soup. And you can always ask me if you are not sure how to do something."

Anna nodded and said, "I love you, mom. Thank you for teaching me and taking care of me. I will help you with other things and ask you if I am not sure. And I will wait until I am older and stronger to cut a radish."

The moral of the story is: Be careful when using sharp tools and ask for help when you need it.

Sammy was so happy and grateful to Lily. He realized that being careless and not paying attention to the trash could be very dangerous for him and his friends. From that day on, Sammy always made sure to keep the beach clean and safe for everyone to enjoy.

Lily heard him and ran to him. She saw his hand was red and swollen. She said, "Oh no, Tom, you have a boo-boo. We need to tell Mommy."

She helped him get up and they went to the house. Mommy saw them and was worried. She said, "What happened, Tom?"

Tom said, "I wanted the flower, but the bee got me. It was hard and sharp."

Mommy said, "I'm sorry, Tom. You are allergic to bees. We need to go to the hospital. They will make you feel better."

She took them to the car and drove to the hospital. There, a nice doctor gave Tom some medicine and a band-aid. He said, "You will be fine, Tom. But you have to be careful with bees. They don't like it when you touch their flowers."

Tom said, "I'm sorry, Mr. Bee. I won't do it again."

Lily said, "I'm glad you are okay, Tom. I love you."

Tom said, "I love you too, Lily. And I love the flowers. But I will look at them, not pick them."

Lily and Ben are friends who like to play outside. They have a big box of toys that they share. They are very organized and always put their toys back in the box when they are done.

One day, they decide to play with their kites. They take their kites out of the box and run to the park. The wind is strong and makes their kites soar high in the sky. They laugh and cheer as they watch their kites fly.

"Look at my kite, Lily!" Ben says. "It is red and blue and has a long tail!"

"Wow, Ben, your kite is very pretty!" Lily says. "My kite is yellow and green and has a star on it!"

They have fun with their kites for a long time. Then they see some clouds in the sky. The clouds are dark and look like they have water in them.

"Oh no, Lily, I think it is going to rain!" Ben says. "We should go back home and put our kites in the box!"

"OK, Ben, let's go!" Lily says. "We don't want our kites to get wet!"

They hurry back to their house and put their kites in the box. They are very organized and make sure the box is closed. They go inside and have a snack. They are happy that they had a good time with their kites. They hope the sun will come out again soon.

Lily and Ben were excited to see the fireworks. They put on their warm coats and hats and went outside with Mom and Dad. They saw many people and cars on the street. They heard loud noises and saw bright colors in the sky.

"Wow, look at that one!" Ben said, pointing at a big red firework that exploded like a flower.

"It's so pretty!" Lily agreed, clapping her hands.

But then a very loud firework made a scary sound, like a lion roaring. Lily jumped and covered her ears. She felt afraid and wanted to go home.

"Mommy, I don't like it!" she cried, hugging Mom's leg.

Mom bent down and comforted Lily. She stroked her hair and kissed her cheek.

"It's okay, sweetie. It's just a noise. It can't hurt you. The fireworks are for fun, not for fear. Do you want to watch them with me?" she asked.

Lily nodded, still feeling a little scared. Mom picked her up and held her close. She pointed at the sky and showed her the different shapes and colors of the fireworks.

"See, that one looks like a star. And that one looks like a heart. And that one looks like a smiley face. Aren't they beautiful?" she said.

Lily smiled and relaxed. She saw that the fireworks were not so bad after all. She liked the star and the heart and the smiley face. She snuggled with Mom and felt fine.

"Mommy, I like the fireworks now. They are pretty and fun. Thank you for comforting me," she said.

Mom hugged her and said, "You're welcome, my love. I'm glad you're fine. You're very brave and smart. I'm proud of you."

They watched the fireworks together until they were over. Then they went home and had hot chocolate and cookies. They said good night and slept well, dreaming of stars and hearts and smiley faces.

One day, Tom and Sue find a new paint. It is shiny and sparkly. It looks like gold. They want to try it. They open the bottle and pour some paint on a paper. They use their brushes to spread it.

"Wow, this paint is so pretty!" Sue says. "It looks like the sun."

"Yes, it does," Tom says. "But it feels funny. It is not soft like the other paints. It is hard and rough."

"Ouch!" Sue says. "This is not paint. This is gold!"

"I don't know," Sue says. "But it is not good for painting. It is too hard and sharp. It can hurt us."

They look at the bottle. It has a label. It says: "Warning: Do not use as paint. This is gold leaf. It can strike your skin and cause cuts. Only use with gloves and scissors."

Tom and Sue do not know what the label means. They only know some of the words. They do not know what leaf, strike, cuts, gloves and scissors are. They are scared. They throw the bottle away. They run to their mom. They show her their fingers. They tell her what happened.

Mom is shocked. She sees the gold on their fingers. She sees the cuts. She sees the bottle. She knows what it is. She is angry. She asks them where they got it.

They tell her they found it in the garage. They thought it was paint. They did not read the label.

Mom takes them to the bathroom. She washes their fingers. She puts bandages on them. She tells them they are lucky. The cuts are not deep. They will heal soon. She tells them they should never use things they do not know. They should always read the label. They should always ask her before they play with something new.

Tom and Sue are sorry. They say they are sorry. They hug mom. They promise they will be careful next time. They learn their lesson. They do not play with gold leaf again. They only play with soft paint.

She picked up Spot and held her gently. She tried to tie the ribbon around Spot's neck, but Spot did not like it. Spot wriggled and meowed and scratched Anna's hand. Anna was surprised and hurt. She let go of Spot and the ribbon.

"Ow, Spot, why did you do that?" Anna asked. She looked at her hand and saw a small cut. She felt sad and angry.

Spot ran away and hid under the bed. She was scared and confused. She did not understand why Anna wanted to put something around her neck. She did not like the ribbon. She wanted to be free and comfortable.

Anna went to her mom and showed her the cut. Her mom cleaned it and put a band-aid on it. She hugged Anna and asked her what happened.

"I wanted to tie a ribbon around Spot's neck, but she scratched me," Anna said.

"Anna, you should not tie anything around Spot's neck. That can hurt her and make her choke. She is a kitten, not a doll. She does not need a ribbon. She needs love and care," her mom said.

"I'm sorry, mom. I did not know. I love Spot. I wanted to make her pretty," Anna said.

"Spot is already pretty, just the way she is. And she loves you too. But you have to respect her and let her be herself. Why don't you go and say sorry to her and play with her?" her mom said.

"Okay, mom. Thank you," Anna said.

Anna went to her room and looked for Spot. She found her under the bed and called her softly. Spot came out and rubbed her head against Anna's leg. Anna bent down and stroked her fur. She said sorry to Spot and gave her a kiss. Spot purred and licked Anna's face. Anna smiled and picked up Spot. She took her to her bed and cuddled her. She forgot about the ribbon. She was happy with her new kitten.

Timmy is confused and disappointed. He does not understand why the skunk is so filthy and why it does not want to be clean and happy. He says, "But mom, it looks so lonely and unhappy. Maybe it just needs a friend. Can I give it some nuts or bread?"

His mom smiles and says, "That is very kind of you, Timmy, but you have to be careful. Skunks are wild animals and they are not used to people. They might bite or scratch you if you get too close. You can leave some nuts or bread on the ground, far away from the skunk, and maybe it will come and eat them. But you have to stay away and watch from a distance. Do you understand?"

Timmy nods and says, "Yes, mom, I understand. I will be careful and stay away. I hope the skunk will like the nuts and bread and feel better soon."

He runs to the bench and gets some nuts and bread from his backpack. He puts them on the ground, far away from the skunk, and waves to it. He says, "Bye bye, skunk. I hope you have a good day. Maybe next time you will be clean and happy like the other squirrels."

He goes back to his mom and hugs her. He says, "Thank you, mom, for teaching me about skunks. They are very different from squirrels, but they are still animals and they deserve respect and kindness."

His mom kisses him and says, "You're welcome, Timmy. You are a very smart and caring boy. I'm proud of you. Now, let's go and play some more in the park. And don't forget to wash your hands before we go home."

They both pulled the crown and tried to take it from each other. They were very angry and loud. They did not see the big dog that was running towards them. The dog liked shiny things. He saw the crown and wanted to have it.

The dog barked and jumped on Lily and Ben. They were scared and let go of the crown. The dog grabbed the crown in his mouth and ran away. Lily and Ben cried and chased the dog, but he was too fast. They lost the crown and the dog.

They were very sad and sorry. They wished they had shared the crown and played nicely. They learned that being greedy and mean can make you lose what you want. They hugged and said, "We are sorry. We are friends. We don't need a crown to have fun." But it was too late. The crown was gone and the dog was happy.

Tim and Jen are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a funny man with a hat and a cane. He is ringing a bell and making jokes.

"Hello, kids! Do you want to see a magic trick?" the funny man says.

"Yes, please!" Tim and Jen say.

The funny man smiles and takes out a big red ball. He throws it in the air and catches it with his cane. Then he throws it again and it disappears.

"Wow!" Tim and Jen say.

"Where did it go?" the funny man asks.

"Is it in your hat?" Tim guesses.

"Is it in your pocket?" Jen asks.

"No, no, no. It is in your ear!" the funny man says. He reaches for Tim's ear and pulls out the ball.

"Ouch!" Tim cries. The ball is not a ball. It is a sharp pin. It hurts Tim's ear and makes it bleed.

"Ha, ha, ha!" the funny man laughs. He is not funny. He is mean. He runs away with his bell and cane.

Tim and Jen are scared and sad. They cry and call for help. A nice lady comes and takes them to the nurse. The nurse puts a bandage on Tim's ear and gives them a hug.

"Who did this to you?" the nurse asks.

"A funny man with a hat and a cane," Tim and Jen say.

"That is not a funny man. That is a bad man. He is a thief and a liar. He hurts people and steals their money. You should stay away from him," the nurse says.

Tim and Jen nod. They learn a lesson. They do not trust strangers. They do not like the funny man with the hat and a cane. He is not funny. He is bad. The end.

Ben and Mia were playing in the garden. They liked to run and jump and swing on the old tire. But they also liked to explore the shed. The shed had many things inside, like tools and pots and cans. Sometimes they found something new and fun to play with.

One day, they saw a big box in the corner of the shed. It was brown and dusty and had a lock on it. Ben and Mia were curious. They wanted to see what was inside the box. They tried to open the lock, but it was too hard. They pulled and pushed and twisted, but nothing happened.

"Maybe we need a key," Ben said.

"Where can we find a key?" Mia asked.

They looked around the shed, but they did not see any keys. They were getting anxious. They wanted to open the box so badly.

Then they heard a noise. It was their mom. She was coming to the shed.

"Ben! Mia! What are you doing in there?" she called.

Ben and Mia were scared. They knew they were not supposed to play in the shed. They tried to hide behind the box, but it was too late. Their mom opened the door and saw them.

"Ben! Mia! How many times have I told you not to go in the shed? It's dangerous! You could hurt yourself or break something!" she scolded.

Ben and Mia felt sorry. They did not mean to make their mom angry. They just wanted to see what was in the box.

"Mom, we're sorry. We just wanted to open the box. It has a lock on it. What's inside?" Ben asked.

Their mom sighed. She looked at the box and smiled.

"That's an old box that belonged to your grandpa. He gave it to me before he passed away. It has some of his things inside, like photos and letters and medals. He was a brave soldier. He fought in a war. He told me to keep the box safe and to only open it when I miss him."

She took out a key from her pocket and unlocked the box. She opened it and showed Ben and Mia the things inside. They saw some black and white photos of a young man in a uniform. He looked like their mom, but with short hair and a hat. They saw some letters with stamps and stickers. They saw some shiny medals with ribbons and stars.

"Wow, these are cool. Can we touch them?" Mia asked.

"Sure, but be gentle. They are very old and precious. These are some of the things that remind me of your grandpa. He was a very kind and brave man. He loved you very much, even though he never met you. He would be proud of you," their mom said.

Ben and Mia felt happy. They liked to see the things that belonged to their grandpa. They felt closer to him. They hugged their mom and thanked her for showing them the box.

They decided to leave the shed and play in the garden. They still liked to run and jump and swing on the old tire. But they also liked to spring to their mom and hug her. They knew she loved them very much, just like their grandpa.

Anna nods. She wants to be friends with the goat. She says, "OK, dad. I will try." She walks slowly to the fence and sits on the grass. She smiles at the goat and says softly, "Hello, goat. I am Anna. I want to play with you. You are not alone. I am here." 

The goat sees Anna and hears her voice. It is curious. It peeks from behind the tree and looks at Anna. It sees that Anna is not loud and scary. She is kind and friendly. It feels less nervous. Anna beams. She says, "Thank you, dad. I love you. And I love Billy. He is my best goat friend."

"Please, can you take us with you?" Sam said. "We are wet and cold and scared."

"We're sorry, we're sorry!" Sam said. "We did not know the water would rise so fast. We just wanted to have fun."

Once upon a time there was a filthy monkey. He liked to spray his friends with water. One day, the monkey was walking through the forest and he saw a pond. He thought it would be fun to spray the water in the pond.

The monkey splashed and sprayed all the water in the pond. Suddenly, he heard a loud noise. When the monkey looked up he saw an elephant who was not happy with the dirty water.

The elephant bellowed and made the monkey scared. The monkey ran away and hid in a tree. The filthy monkey sprayed water on the elephant but the elephant didn't care. He just sprayed water back, and the monkey had to run away.

The monkey ran home and he was never, ever, brave enough to spray water again!

Then, they saw a lady walking by. She had long, white hair and a kind smile. She looked very old, but also very beautiful. She saw Lila and Tom and said, "Hello, children. What are you doing?"

Lila and Tom told her about Ben and the monkey bars and wisdom. They asked her, "Do you know what wisdom is? Do you have wisdom?"

The lady nodded and said, "Yes, I know what wisdom is. And yes, I have wisdom. But wisdom is not what Ben told you. Wisdom is not when you know everything and you are always right. Wisdom is when you learn from everything and you are always kind. Wisdom is not when you are big and strong and smart. Wisdom is when you are humble and gentle and brave. Wisdom is not something you get by pushing others away. Wisdom is something you get by helping others along. Wisdom is not something you have. Wisdom is something you share."

Lila and Tom listened to the lady and felt a warm feeling in their hearts. They understood what she meant. They realized that Ben was not wise at all. He was mean and rude and selfish. They decided that they did not want to be like Ben. They wanted to be like the lady. They wanted to have wisdom.

They thanked the lady and gave her a hug. They said, "You are very wise and very beautiful. We want to be wise and beautiful too. Can you teach us how to be wise and beautiful?"

The lady smiled and said, "Of course, I can. But you already have wisdom and beauty inside you. You just need to let them shine. Come, let's go to the monkey bars. I will show you how to hang and how to share."

Lila and Tom followed the lady to the monkey bars. They saw Ben still hanging there, alone and bored. They asked him, "Do you want to play with us? We have a new friend. She is very wise and very beautiful. She can teach us all how to be wise and beautiful too."

Ben looked at them and at the lady. He felt curious and confused. He wondered what they were talking about. He said, "OK, I will play with you. But who is she? And what is wisdom? And what is beautiful?"

The lady said, "I am a grandma. And wisdom is when you learn from everything and you are always kind. And beautiful is when you are humble and gentle and brave. And you can be wise and beautiful too, if you want to. Come, let me show you."

And so, Lila and Tom and Ben and the grandma played together on the monkey bars. They hung and swung and laughed and talked. They learned and shared and helped and cared. They became friends and had fun. And they all felt wise and beautiful.

Tom had an idea. He found a long rod in his house. He thought he could use the rod to separate Jerry from his hiding place. Tom said, "If I can't catch Jerry, I can use this rod to make him come out."

Tom tried to poke the rod into Jerry's hiding place, but Jerry was too quick. He ran out from the other side and started to laugh. "You can't catch me, lazy Tom!" said Jerry.

Tom felt sad and upset. He knew he needed to be more active and not be lazy anymore. From that day on, Tom decided to play and run every day. He wanted to be fast like Jerry and not be a lazy cat anymore. And soon, Tom and Jerry became good friends who loved to play and run together.

Sam and Lily did not want to clean up. They wanted to keep playing. They pouted and whined.

"But dad, we were having fun!" Sam said.

"Yeah, dad, we don't like cleaning!" Lily said.

Sam and Lily followed their dad's instructions. They worked together and helped each other. They realized that cleaning was not so bad, it was actually kind of fun. They made jokes and sang songs as they cleaned.

Soon, the garage was neat and tidy. Their dad smiled. He was proud of them.

Sam and Lily smiled. They felt good.

"Of course you can, kids. But remember, next time, clean up after yourselves. Deal?" he said.

"Deal!" Sam and Lily said.

They ran to the basket and grabbed their cars. They zoomed them around the garage again, but this time, they were careful not to make a mess. They were happy and proud.

Lila was a girl who liked to eat ice cream. She had a big spoon that she used to scoop the ice cream from the bowl. She loved her spoon very much and never let anyone else use it.

One day, Lila went to the park with her mom and dad. They bought her a cone of ice cream from the truck. Lila was happy, but she wanted to use her spoon to eat the ice cream. She asked her mom to get her spoon from the bag.

"Sorry, Lila, I forgot to bring your spoon," her mom said. "You can use the cone instead. It's yummy and crunchy."

Lila was angry. She did not want to use the cone. She wanted to use her spoon. She saw a boy sitting on a bench with a bowl of ice cream and a spoon. She ran to him and snatched his spoon.

"Hey, that's my spoon!" the boy cried. "Give it back!"

"No, it's mine now!" Lila said. "You can have my cone. It's a fair trade."

Lila ran away with the spoon, leaving the boy with her cone. She was happy for a moment, until she realized that the spoon was not hers. It was smaller and duller than her spoon. It did not fit in her hand or in her mouth. It did not make her ice cream taste better. It was a bad spoon.

She looked for her cone, but it was too late. The boy had thrown it away in the trash. He was sad and angry. He did not like cones. He liked spoons. He had a rare spoon that his grandma had given him. It was shiny and smooth and had a funny shape. It was a special spoon.

Lila felt sorry for the boy. She wanted to give him back his spoon and say sorry. But she could not find him. He had gone away with his mom and dad. Lila was left with a bad spoon and no ice cream. She was sad and angry. She had made a bad choice.

The moral of the story is: Do not take things that are not yours. You might lose something that you love and hurt someone else. Be happy with what you have and share with others.

But the turtle did not come out. Lily had an idea. She picked some flowers and leaves and made a necklace. She threw the necklace into the pond and said, "This is for you, turtle. It is pretty and colorful. We made it for you."

The turtle saw the necklace and was curious. It poked its head out of the water and looked at the necklace. It liked the necklace. It swam closer and took the necklace with its mouth. It put the necklace around its neck and smiled.

"Thank you, Tom and Lily," the turtle said. "You are very kind. I like your gift. You can be my friends."

Tom and Lily were happy. They had made a new friend. They clapped their hands and cheered. They had completed their mission. They had made the turtle feel normal and welcome. They played with the turtle for a long time, until it was time to go home. They waved goodbye to the turtle and promised to come back soon. The turtle waved back and thanked them again. It was a good day for everyone.

"Why is he doing that?" Mia asked.

"Maybe the tree is thirsty," Ben said.

"No, silly. Trees don't drink water like that. They drink water from the ground," Mia said.

"Like what?" Mia asked.

"Like remind. Do you know what remind means?" Ben asked.

"Remind means to help someone remember something. For example, my mom reminds me to brush my teeth every night," Ben said.

"Sure, I can remind you. Let's go to the slide after we watch the truck," Ben said.

"Ben, Lily, what are you doing?" their mom asked, surprised. "Why are you mailing a dish with flour on it?"

Ben and Lily stopped and looked at their mom. They realized they had been careless. They had used a real dish and real flour, not their toy ones. They had made a mess in the kitchen and wasted the stamps.

"Sorry, mom," they said together. "We were playing chefs and we wanted to mail a cake to Sam."

Timmy felt a little better after the doctor's visit. He thanked his mommy for calling the doctor and for taking care of him. He cuddled with his teddy bear and fell asleep. He dreamed of being lively and playing with his friends again.

Ben was an adventurous boy. He liked to explore new places and try new things. One day, he saw a big table in the kitchen. It had many things on it: plates, cups, forks, spoons, napkins, and a big cake.

Ben wanted to see the cake. He climbed on a chair and reached for it. But he was too small. He could not touch the cake. He stretched his arm more and more. Then, he lost his balance. He fell off the chair and knocked over the table. All the things on the table fell down too. There was a big mess.

Ben was scared. He heard his mom coming. He did not want to get in trouble. He looked around and saw a cloth. He grabbed it and tried to wipe the mess. But he could not wipe it all. The cloth was too small. The cake was too big. The mess was too much.

Mom came into the kitchen. She saw Ben and the mess. She was not happy. She said, "Ben, what did you do? You made a big mess. You should not climb on the table. You could get hurt. And you wasted the cake. It was for your sister's birthday."

Ben felt sorry. He said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I wanted to see the cake. I was adventurous. I did not mean to make a mess. I tried to wipe it. But I could not."

Mom sighed. She said, "I know you were adventurous, Ben. But you have to be careful too. And you have to ask before you touch things. Now, help me clean up this mess. And then, we will make a new cake for your sister. OK?"

Ben nodded. He said, "OK, Mom. I will help you. And I will say sorry to my sister. And I will not climb on the table again."

Mom smiled. She said, "Thank you, Ben. I love you. You are my adventurous boy. But sometimes, you have to be a good boy too."

Tim and Lily were playing with blocks in their room. They liked to build tall towers and bridges with the blocks. They had many colors of blocks: red, blue, yellow, green, and orange.

"Look, Lily, I made an orange bridge!" Tim said, showing his sister his creation.

"That's nice, Tim. But I made a bigger tower!" Lily said, pointing to her stack of blocks. "It is taller than you!"

Tim wanted to make his bridge taller too. He reached for more blocks on the shelf. But he was not careful. He grabbed too many blocks and they fell from his hand.

"Oops!" Tim said, as the blocks hit the floor. "I drop the blocks!"

But the blocks were not the only thing that fell. The floor started to shake and rumble. The shelves and the pictures on the wall moved and tipped over. The bed and the dresser slid and bumped. The toys and the books flew and crashed.

"What is that?" Lily asked, scared. "Why is everything moving?"

"It is an earthquake!" Tim said, remembering what their mom had told them. "We have to go under the table!"

Tim and Lily ran to the table and crawled under it. They held each other and waited for the earthquake to stop. They hoped their mom and dad were safe too.

After a few minutes, the shaking stopped. The room was very messy. The blocks and the other things were everywhere. Tim and Lily peeked out from under the table.

"Are you okay, Lily?" Tim asked.

"I'm okay, Tim. Are you okay?" Lily asked.

"I'm okay, Lily. But look at our blocks. They are all broken and mixed up."

"That's okay, Tim. We can build new things with them. Maybe we can make an orange earthquake!" Lily said, trying to cheer up her brother.

Tim smiled. He liked his sister's idea. He hugged her and said, "You are the best, Lily. Let's make an orange earthquake!"

One day, a fat king was very bored. He had a big crown, but no friends to play with. He called his servant and said, "Bring me someone to make me happy."

The servant nodded and ran away. He looked for someone who could make the king happy. He saw a clown, a singer, a dancer, and a painter. But he thought they were too silly, too loud, too fast, and too messy. He wanted to find someone who was smart and good.

He walked and walked until he came to a small house. He knocked on the door and a girl opened it. She had a bright smile and a kind face. The servant asked, "Can you make the king happy?"

The girl shrugged and said, "I don't know. What does he like?"

The servant said, "He likes nothing. He is very bored and lonely. He has a big crown, but no friends."

The girl said, "That is sad. Maybe I can try to make him happy. But I have nothing to give him. Only this flower that I picked from the garden."

The servant said, "That is enough. Come with me."

They went to the palace and met the king. The king looked at the girl and said, "Who are you? What can you do for me?"

The girl said, "I am just a girl. I have nothing to do for you. Only this flower that I picked from the garden. It is for you."

The king took the flower and smelled it. He felt a warm feeling in his heart. He smiled and said, "Thank you. This is the most beautiful thing I have ever seen. What is your name?"

The girl said, "My name is Rose."

The king said, "Rose, you have made me happy. Will you be my friend?"

Rose said, "Yes, I will be your friend."

The king and Rose became friends. They played and talked and laughed together. The king learned to enjoy the simple things in life. He shared his crown with Rose and gave her a hug. He was not bored and lonely anymore. He was happy and grateful.

The moral of the story is: Happiness is not found in things, but in people. A friend is more precious than a crown. A flower is more beautiful than gold.

Lily was a very independent girl. She liked to do things by herself, without help from anyone. She liked to climb trees, make mud pies, and play with her dog, Spot.

One day, Lily found a rope in the garage. She had an idea. She tied one end of the rope to a branch of a big tree, and the other end to a bucket. She wanted to make a swing. She put some rocks in the bucket to make it heavy, and then she climbed on the branch. She pushed the bucket with her foot, and the rope made the bucket swing back and forth. Lily laughed and swung with the bucket.

But Lily did not see that the rope was old and weak. It had some holes and tears in it. And she did not see that the bucket was too close to the fire pit, where her dad had burned some leaves and sticks. The fire was still hot and had some sparks.

As Lily swung with the bucket, the rope rubbed against the branch and the fire pit. The rope started to burn. It made a hissing sound and a bad smell. Lily did not notice. She was having too much fun.

But Spot noticed. He saw the smoke and the flames. He barked and ran to Lily. He jumped on the branch and bit the rope. He pulled and pulled, until the rope broke. The bucket fell to the ground, and the rocks spilled out. Lily fell too, but Spot caught her in his mouth. He carried her to the grass, and licked her face. Lily was scared and surprised. She hugged Spot and thanked him. He saved her from the burning rope.

Lily learned a lesson. She realized that being independent is good, but sometimes she needs to be careful and listen to others. She also realized that Spot is her best friend. She gave him a big bone and a kiss. They played together, away from the fire pit and the rope.

Her mom came into the room and saw what happened. "Don't worry, Lily," her mom said. "Let's see if we can fix it."

They got some glue and tried to put the teapot back together, but it was too heavy and kept falling over. 

"I can't balance it," Lily said sadly.

Her mom had an idea. "Let's use a teaspoon to balance the teapot," she said. 

They carefully placed the teaspoon under the teapot and it worked! The teapot was balanced and didn't fall over anymore. Lily was so happy that her favorite tea set was fixed.

Lily didn't understand why chocolate was bad for her, so she asked her mom to explain.

Her mom said, "Too much chocolate can make you wild and hyper, and it's not good for your teeth."

Lily didn't listen to her mom and snuck the chocolate bar into her room. She ate the whole thing and became very wild and hyper. But then, she started to feel sick and had to go to the hospital.

The moral of the story is that sometimes we need to listen to our parents, even if we don't understand why they say no. Eating too much chocolate can be bad for us, and it's important to be careful with what we eat.

One day, he saw a big package by the door. It had his name on it. He wondered what was inside. He wanted to open it and see. But mommy and daddy said no. They said it was a surprise for his birthday. They said he had to wait until tomorrow. Tommy was sad and curious. He wanted to know what was in the package.

He waited until mommy and daddy were busy. He sneaked to the door. He looked at the package. He touched it. He shook it. He heard something rattle. He felt something soft. He smelled something sweet. He decided to open it. He ripped the paper. He opened the box. He saw a big teddy bear. He smiled. He hugged it. He smelled it. It smelled like honey. He loved it.

But then he heard mommy and daddy coming. He panicked. He knew he had done something bad. He knew he had spoiled the surprise. He felt guilty. He looked for a place to hide. He saw the pool. He ran to the pool. He threw the teddy bear in the pool. He jumped in after it. He hoped mommy and daddy would not see.

But mommy and daddy saw everything. They saw the package by the door. They saw the paper on the floor. They saw the box on the grass. They saw the teddy bear in the water. They saw Tommy diving in the pool. They were angry and worried. They ran to the pool. They shouted at Tommy.

"Tommy, what have you done? Why did you open the package? Why did you throw the teddy bear in the pool? Don't you know it can get ruined? Don't you know it can be dangerous? Don't you know we love you and want to make you happy?"

Tommy came out of the water. He looked at mommy and daddy. He saw their faces. He felt their words. He was sorry. He cried. He said, "I'm sorry, mommy and daddy. I was curious. I wanted to see. I wanted to dive. I didn't mean to be bad. I didn't mean to make you sad. I love you and the teddy bear. Can you forgive me?"

Mommy and daddy looked at Tommy. They saw his tears. They heard his voice. They felt his heart. They were still angry and worried. But they were also kind and loving. They hugged Tommy. They said, "We forgive you, Tommy. We know you were curious. We know you wanted to dive. We know you didn't mean to be bad. We know you love us and the teddy bear. We love you too, Tommy. You have to promise us to be careful and listen to us. Can you promise us that?"

Tommy nodded. He said, "I promise, mommy and daddy. I promise to never open a package without permission. I promise to never throw anything in the pool. I promise to be careful and listen to you. Thank you for forgiving me. Thank you for loving me. Thank you for the teddy bear. Can we dry it and keep it?"

Tommy smiled. He said, "I understand, mommy and daddy. I'm happy. I have a diving teddy bear. I have the best mommy and daddy. I have the best birthday. Can we dive now?"

Lily was hurt by their words. She hugged Anna and cried. She ran back to her mom and said, "Mom, they are mean! They said bad things about Anna! They don't like her!"

Lily's mom hugged her and said, "Lily, I'm sorry they hurt your feelings. But you know, you were not very nice to them either. You should not say that your doll is the best and their toys are not. That is not humble. That is proud and rude. You should be humble and kind. You should say nice things about their toys and share your doll with them. Maybe then they will like you and Anna more."

Lily thought about what her mom said. She realized that she was wrong. She said, "Mom, you are right. I was not humble and kind. I'm sorry. I will try to be a better parent to Anna and a better friend to the other children. Can we go back and say sorry to them and play with them?"

Lily's mom smiled and said, "Yes, we can. I'm proud of you, Lily. You are a good girl and a good parent to Anna. Come on, let's go and have fun with the other children."

Ben and Lily were mice who lived in a big house. They liked to find cheese in the kitchen and bring it to their hole. But the house had a cat who liked to chase them. The cat was big and mean and had sharp teeth.

One day, Ben and Lily saw a new cheese on the table. It was yellow and round and smelled very good. They wanted to try it, but the cat was sleeping on the chair next to the table. Ben said, "We have to be brave and get the cheese. It looks yummy."

Lily said, "But the cat will wake up and catch us. He is faster and stronger than us. We should wait until he goes away."

Ben said, "No, we can't wait. The cheese might be gone by then. Someone might eat it or sell it. We have to be smart and sneaky. I have a plan."

Ben told Lily his plan. They found a ball of yarn and a bell. They tied the bell to the yarn and dragged it to the other side of the kitchen. Then they rang the bell and hid behind the cupboard.

The cat heard the bell and opened his eyes. He saw the yarn and the bell and thought it was a toy. He jumped off the chair and ran to the yarn. He played with it and forgot about the cheese.

Ben and Lily saw their chance and ran to the table. They grabbed the cheese and ran back to their hole. They made it safely and shared the cheese. It was delicious.

They were very happy and proud. They had been brave and smart and got the cheese. They said, "We are the best cheese hunters ever!"

She heard a noise from the living room. She ran there and saw her brother Max. He was holding her diary and turning the pages. He was laughing at her pictures and words.

"Max, give me my diary!" Lily shouted. "That is mine, not yours!"

Max looked at her and smirked. "No, I want to read it. It is funny. You write like a baby."

Lily felt more sad and angry. She tried to grab her diary, but Max was bigger and stronger. He pushed her away and ran to his room. He locked the door behind him.

Lily knocked on the door and cried. "Max, please, be polite. Give me back my diary. It is not nice to take things that are not yours."

Max did not answer. He kept reading and laughing.

Lily did not know what to do. She felt like giving up. But then she had an idea. She remembered that Max had a diary too. He wrote in it every night. He kept it in a drawer in his desk.

Lily sneaked into his room when he was not there. She found his diary and took it. She opened it and read it. She saw that Max wrote about his crush, his fears, and his dreams. She felt sorry for him. He was not so different from her.

She decided to do something nice. She wrote a note in his diary. She wrote: "Dear Max, I am sorry that you took my diary. I know that you are curious and bored. But it is not polite to read other people's diaries. They are private and special. I hope you will give me back my diary soon. I also hope you will be happy and brave. I love you, your sister Lily."

She put his diary back in the drawer. She hoped that he would read her note and understand.

The next day, Lily found her diary on her bed. There was a note on it. It said: "Dear Lily, I am sorry that I took your diary. I was curious and bored. But you are right, it is not polite to read other people's diaries. They are private and special. I hope you will forgive me. I also hope you will be happy and creative. I love you, your brother Max."

Lily smiled and hugged her diary. She felt happy and grateful. She wrote a new page in her diary. She wrote: "Today, Max and I learned a lesson. We learned to respect each other's diaries. We also learned to be polite and kind. We are still brother and sister, but we are also friends."

One day, when her dad was out, Lily saw a big toy on his desk. It had a long tube and a round glass and a shiny light. She climbed on a chair and looked at the toy. She saw a small slide with a drop of water on it. She put her eye on the round glass and turned the light on. She gasped.

The moral of the story is: Be honest and respectful. Do not steal. Listen to your parents and siblings. Be grateful for what you have.

After they mixed it all up, mommy let Timmy feed the batter into the cake pan. They put it in the oven and waited patiently for it to bake. 

When it was done, they took it out and let it cool. Timmy was so excited to try the cake he helped make. It was delicious! From that day on, Timmy loved to help his mommy in the kitchen and make yummy treats together.

Lily felt angry and wanted to slap him for being rude. But then she remembered her mom's words: "Always be kind and share with others." So, she smiled and gave him a piece of cake. Timmy saw what she did and came over to thank her. From that day on, they became even closer friends. The moral of the story is to always be kind and share, even if you feel distant from someone.

When they got home, Lily's mom told her that it's always important to help others. She also reminded her that it's never okay to use harsh words with people. Lily agreed and went to bed, dreaming of all the ways she could help others when she grows up.

Once upon a time, there was a wise owl who lived in the east. Every day, he would sit on a tree and watch the world go by. One day, a little rabbit came hopping by.

"Hello, Mr. Owl," said the rabbit. "What are you doing?"

"I'm just watching the world," replied the owl. "Would you like to join me?"

The rabbit hopped up onto the tree and sat next to the wise owl. "Wow, this is a great view," said the rabbit.

"Yes, it is," said the owl. "Look, the sun is starting to bow down towards the horizon. It's almost time for me to go to sleep."

The rabbit hopped down from the tree and said goodbye to the owl. "Goodnight, Mr. Owl," he said. "Thank you for letting me join you."

"Goodnight, little rabbit," said the owl. "Sleep well."
