But as the sun began to set, Max realized he was getting hungry. He searched for some fruit to eat, but all he found was a bitter lemon. He didn't like it, but he knew he had to eat something. 

As he climbed up to his treehouse to sleep, he heard some rustling in the bushes. Max was scared. He thought it might be a dangerous animal. But then he remembered his treehouse and climbed up to safety. The next morning, he saw that his treehouse had protected him from a big, scary tiger. Max was so happy he had built his treehouse!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat his dinner on a big, blue plate. One day, Timmy was running around the house and he stumbled over a toy. He fell and his plate went flying into the air. It crashed onto the ground and broke into a million pieces. Timmy was sad because he loved his plate.

But then, Timmy's mom came over and gave him a big hug. She told him that it was okay and that the plate was just a thing. It was harmless and could be replaced. Timmy learned that things are not as important as people and that accidents happen. He felt better and knew that he could always get a new plate. 

From that day on, Timmy was more careful when he was running around the house. He didn't want to stumble and break anything else. He also learned that things can be replaced, but people cannot. Timmy was happy and grateful for his mom's love and wisdom.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a magic cube. This cube could appear and disappear when you called its name. One day, a little boy named Tim found the cube while playing outside. He was very happy and took it home.

Tim showed the cube to his friends. They all wanted to play with it. But Tim felt ashamed because he knew he should share, but he wanted to keep the cube for himself. He told his friends they couldn't play with it.

The next day, Tim went to the park with the cube. He wanted to make the cube appear and disappear to show everyone how special it was. But when he called the cube's name, nothing happened. He tried again and again, but the cube wouldn't listen.

Tim felt sad and alone. He realized that by not sharing the cube with his friends, he had lost them too. In the end, the magic cube disappeared forever, and Tim was left with no friends and no magic cube.

The moral of the story is that sharing is important. If you don't share, you might end up losing what you have and the people you care about.

"Can we go to the tree, Mom?" Ben asked.

"Yes, but be polite to the bees. They work hard to make honey. Don't touch them or make them angry," Mom said.

Ben and Lily nodded and ran to the tree. They smelled the flowers and watched the bees. They saw a big hive with honey dripping from it.

"Wow, look at the honey! It must be yummy!" Lily said.

"I want some honey. Can we take some?" Ben said.

"No, Ben. That's the bees' honey. They need it for their home. It's not polite to take it," Lily said.

But Ben did not listen. He reached for the hive and tried to grab some honey. The bees saw him and got angry. They buzzed and stung him.

"Ow, ow, ow! The bees are hurting me!" Ben cried.

Lily ran to get Mom. Mom came and helped Ben. She put some ice on his stings and gave him a hug.

"I'm sorry, Mom. I was not polite to the bees. I wanted their honey," Ben said.

"It's okay, Ben. You learned your lesson. The bees succeed in making honey because they work together and share. We should respect them and their honey," Mom said.

"Can we still watch the bees, Mom?" Lily asked.

"Yes, but from a safe distance. And maybe we can have some honey later, from our own jar," Mom said.

Ben and Lily smiled and thanked Mom. They watched the bees from afar and learned more about them. They were polite to the bees and the bees were polite to them.

They pressed some buttons and the cube made noises and flashed. They laughed and clapped their hands. They pressed more buttons and the cube changed colors and shapes. They gasped and cheered. They pressed more and more buttons and the cube became bigger and bigger. They were amazed and excited.

But then, something went wrong. The cube became too big and filled the whole room. It pushed the twins against the wall and blocked the door and the window. It made loud and scary noises and flashed red and black. The twins were scared and cried. They wanted to get out and call for help, but they could not.

They hugged each other and said, "We are sorry, we were greedy and curious. We should have left the cube alone. We should have been happy with our own cubes. We should have listened to mom and dad. They told us not to touch things in the attic. They know what is best for us."

The cube heard their words and felt sorry for them. It realized that it had become too big and dangerous. It wanted to be a toy, not a trap. It wanted to make the twins happy, not sad. It decided to change back to its normal size and let them go.

It pressed its own buttons and became smaller and smaller. It stopped making noises and flashing. It became a shiny cube again. It rolled to the twins and said, "I am sorry, I was silly and playful. I should have been careful and gentle. I should have respected your space and your things. I should have listened to you and your feelings. You are my friends and I care for you."

The twins were surprised and relieved. They thanked the cube and said, "We are sorry, too. We were not silly or playful. We were rude and selfish. We should have been careful and gentle, too. We should have respected you and your buttons. We should have listened to you and your noises. You are our friend and we care for you, too."

They all hugged and laughed. The cube became a rainbow and the room became bright. They played with the cube and their own cubes. They built towers, castles, cars and animals. They had fun together.

The moral of the story is: Be careful and gentle, respect and listen, share and enjoy. You can be happy with what you have and who you are. You can make friends with anyone and anything. You can become anything and anyone.

But they did not know that their grandpa was in the kitchen too. He was deaf and he could not hear them. He wanted to make some tea and he opened the cupboard door. He was surprised to see Ben and Mia inside.

"Hello, my little sailors," he said. "What are you doing in there?"

Ben and Mia were scared. They thought he was a pirate who wanted to steal their ship. They shouted, "Shiver me timbers! It's the enemy! Quick, hide the treasure!"

They grabbed the flag, the map and the telescope and ran out of the cupboard. They left the toy parrot behind. Grandpa laughed and picked up the parrot. He said, "Don't worry, I'm not a pirate. I'm your grandpa. Do you want some tea?"

The parrot said, "Polly wants a cracker!" Grandpa smiled and gave the parrot a cracker. He said, "You're a clever bird. Maybe you can teach me some sailor words."

Tom and Lily are twins. They like to play in the garden. They run, jump, and laugh. They see a big tree with red apples. They want to pick some apples for mom.

"Look, Lily, there is a big apple up there. I can reach it if I shake the branch," Tom says.

He climbs on the tree and holds the branch. He shakes it hard. The apple falls down. But so does Tom. He lands on the grass with a thud.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom cries. He hurts his arm and his leg.

Lily runs to him and hugs him. "Are you okay, Tom? You were careless. You should be careful on the tree," she says.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I wanted to get the apple for mom. But I shook the branch too much. It was too strong," Tom says.

Lily helps him get up. She sees a cut on his arm. She takes a leaf and wraps it around his arm. "There, that will make it better. Come on, let's go inside. Mom will give you a hug and a kiss. And maybe a cookie," she says.

They walk to the house, holding the apple. Mom sees them and smiles. She sees Tom's arm and his leg. She frowns.

"What happened, my darlings? Did you have an accident?" she asks.

Tom and Lily tell her what happened. Mom hugs them and says, "I'm glad you are not badly hurt. But you should be more careful, Tom. Shaking the branch was not a good idea. You could have fallen on something sharp or hard. You are lucky it was only grass."

She takes them to the bathroom. She turns on the shower. She washes their faces and hands. She cleans Tom's cut and puts a band-aid on it. She rubs some cream on his leg.

"There, you are all clean and cozy. Now, let's go to the kitchen. I have some apple pie for you. You can share the apple you picked with me. It looks very yummy," she says.

Tom and Lily smile. They love mom. They love apple pie. They are happy. They learned a lesson. They will not shake the branch again. They will be careful.

Lily was hungry and curious. She sniffed the cheese and thought it smelled good. She was about to bite it, when she heard a voice.

"Lily, stop! Don't eat that!" It was her mother, who had followed her to the garden. She saw the rat and the poison and knew what was going on. She ran to Lily and pushed her away from the cheese. She hissed at the rat and chased it away.

They are mean and sneaky. And you should never follow a stranger. They might want to hurt you. You should always stay close to me and listen to me. I love you and I want to keep you safe."

Lily felt sorry and ashamed. She realized she had been foolish and careless. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I was wrong. I won't follow a stranger again. I will stay with you and listen to you. I love you too, mom."

Lily nodded and followed her mother home. She learned a valuable lesson that day. She learned to be wary of strangers and to trust her mother. She learned that not everything that looks good is good, and that some things can be poison. She learned to be a smart and safe cat.

"Thank you, Ben," she said. "You are very kind. I'm sorry the dog took your mitten."

Lily and Ben held hands and walked home. They still felt sad about their snowman, but they were glad they had each other. They did not suffer anymore.

Ben and the bug started to fight. They shouted and chased each other. They did not see the branch breaking. They did not hear the crack. They did not feel the fall. They only felt the pain and the shock.

Mia heard the noise. She saw Ben and the bug falling from the tree. She felt worried and sorry. She ran to them and said, "Oh, Ben, oh, bug. Are you okay? You are hurt and bleeding. You should not fight. You should be friends. I will help you and hug you."

Ben and the bug looked at Mia. They looked at each other. They felt ashamed and sorry. They said, "Thank you, Mia. You are kind and sweet. You are our friend. We are sorry for being rude and mean. We should not climb and sting. We should play and share. Can you forgive us and join us?"

Mia smiled and nodded. She said, "Yes, I can. I am glad you are okay. I love you both. Let us go to the house and get some bandages and cookies. Then we can play with the ball and have some fun."

Ben and the bug agreed and followed Mia. They held her hands and said, "We love you too, Mia. You are the best. You are the queen of the garden. You can teach us how to be nice and happy." They all laughed and walked to the house. They learned a lesson and became friends.

Mama heard the noise and came to Sara's room. She saw Sara playing with the pot and the soup. She was angry and scared. She yelled at Sara to quit. She took the pot away from Sara and put it back in the kitchen.

"Look, Sam, a red car! Let's go and see it!" Ben says.

"OK, Ben, but be careful. We don't know who owns it. Maybe they will be angry if we touch it." Sam says.

"Wow, look at this! A bag and a phone! Maybe there is money and candy in the bag. Let's take it!" Ben says.

"No, Ben, that is wrong. That is stealing. We can't take what is not ours. That is bad. Let's go back." Sam says.

Suddenly, they hear a loud noise. It is a siren. It is a police car. The police car stops near them. A police officer gets out. He sees Ben and Sam with the bag and the phone. He is angry.

"Hey, you two! What are you doing with that bag and that phone? That is not yours. That is from the red car. That is a stolen car. You are in big trouble!" The police officer says.

"Ben, Sam, how could you do this? You know stealing is wrong. You could have hurt yourself or someone else. You could have gone to jail. Jail is a bad place. You don't want to go there. You have to say sorry and give back what you took. You have to learn from your mistake." Their parents say.

Ben and Sam feel very sorry. They cry and say sorry. They give back the bag and the phone. They promise to never steal again. They go home with their parents. They are not happy. They are ashamed.

The moral of the story is: Stealing is wrong. It can get you in trouble and make you unhappy. You should respect other people's things and be honest.

Tom was a little boy who liked to whistle. He whistled all the time, even when he was in bed. He whistled so loud that he woke up his sister, Lily, who slept in the next room.

"Tom, stop whistling!" Lily said. "I want to sleep!"

But Tom did not stop. He whistled even louder, because he thought it was fun. He did not care that Lily was angry and tired.

One night, Tom heard a strange noise outside his window. He was scared. He stopped whistling and looked out. He saw a big, dark shape with two bright eyes. It was an unknown animal. It looked like a big dog, but it was not a dog. It was a wolf.

The wolf heard Tom's whistling and came to his window. It wanted to eat Tom. It growled and scratched the glass. Tom was very afraid. He wished he had not whistled so much. He wished he had listened to Lily.

He ran to Lily's room and knocked on her door. "Lily, Lily, help me!" he cried. "There is a wolf outside my window!"

Lily opened the door and saw Tom's face. He was pale and shaking. She felt sorry for him. She hugged him and said, "Don't worry, Tom. I will help you. Come, sleep with me. We will be safe."

She took Tom to her bed and covered him with a blanket. She whispered, "The wolf can't get in. The window is locked. The wolf will go away soon. You are brave, Tom. I love you."

Tom felt better. He thanked Lily and said, "I love you too, Lily. I am sorry I whistled so much. I was silly. I will not whistle at night anymore. I will let you sleep."

Lily smiled and said, "That's okay, Tom. I forgive you. You are a good brother. You can whistle in the day, but not in the night. The night is for sleeping and dreaming."

They cuddled and closed their eyes. They fell asleep and had sweet dreams. The wolf left and never came back.

The moral of the story is: Be respectful of others and don't make noise when they are sleeping. You never know what dangers might lurk in the dark.

The moral of the story is: Don't be jealous or mean. Be kind and honest. And try to do your best, not your fastest.

Moral: Do not take what is not yours. Be honest and share. Friendship is more important than toys.

Lily and Max were twins who liked to play in the garden. One day, they saw a big orange pumpkin growing on a vine. They wanted to pick it and make a pie.

"Let's ask Mommy if we can have the pumpkin," Lily said.

"Okay," Max agreed.

They ran to the house and found Mommy in the kitchen. She was busy making lunch.

"Mommy, Mommy, can we have the pumpkin in the garden?" Lily asked.

Mommy looked at them and smiled. "The pumpkin is not ready yet, my dears. It needs more time to grow and become ripe. If you pick it now, it will be hard and bitter."

"But we want to make a pie," Max said.

"I know, sweetie, but you have to wait. Maybe in a few weeks, the pumpkin will be ready. Then we can make a pie together. How does that sound?"

Lily and Max felt sad. They really wanted the pumpkin.

"Can we at least look at it?" Lily asked.

"Sure, you can look at it, but don't touch it, okay?" Mommy said.

"Okay," Lily and Max said.

They went back to the garden and saw the pumpkin. It was big and round and shiny. They wished they could have it.

Then they saw a grumpy cat sitting next to the pumpkin. The cat had black fur and yellow eyes. It looked angry and mean.

"Go away, this is my pumpkin," the cat hissed.

Lily and Max were scared. They didn't like the cat.

"Who are you?" Max asked.

"I'm Fluffy, and this is my pumpkin. I found it first, and I'm going to eat it," the cat said.

"But it's not your pumpkin, it's Mommy's pumpkin. She planted it and watered it and cared for it," Lily said.

"I don't care, it's mine now. And you can't have it. Go away, or I'll scratch you," the cat said.

Lily and Max didn't know what to do. They wanted to be nice, but they also wanted the pumpkin.

"Maybe we can share the pumpkin," Lily said. "We can offer you some pie, if you let us have some pumpkin."

The cat thought for a moment. He liked pie, but he also liked pumpkin.

"Fine, I'll share the pumpkin with you, but only if you give me half of the pie," the cat said.

"Okay, deal," Lily and Max said.

They shook paws with the cat and became friends. They decided to wait for the pumpkin to be ready, and then make a pie with Mommy. They hoped the pie would be yummy and not make them grumpy.

One day, a brown dog was walking in the park. He saw a big, shiny car with a flag on it. He ran to the car and barked. He wanted to see who was inside.

"Who are you?" a voice asked from the car. The dog looked up and saw a lady with a crown and a dress. She was the queen.

"I am a dog," the dog said. "I like to run and play. What are you?"

"I am the queen," the lady said. "I rule the land. I have to go to a meeting. Please mind the car while I am gone."

The dog nodded. He liked the queen. She was nice and pretty. He sat by the car and waited for her to come back.

Soon, a cat came by. The cat was black and sneaky. He saw the car and wanted to scratch it. He jumped on the hood and dug his claws.

"Hey, stop that!" the dog shouted. He ran to the cat and chased him away. "This is the queen's car. You cannot hurt it."

The cat hissed and ran. He did not like the dog. He did not like the queen. He did not like the car.

The dog was proud. He had minded the car. He had protected it from the cat. He wagged his tail and smiled.

The queen came back. She saw the dog and the car. She saw the scratch marks on the hood. She was sad.

"Oh, no," she said. "What happened to my car?"

The dog told her what he had done. He told her about the cat and the chase. He told her he was sorry.

The queen smiled. She was not angry. She was grateful.

"Thank you, dog," she said. "You are a good and brave dog. You minded the car very well. You saved it from more damage. You are a hero."

She gave the dog a hug and a treat. She invited him to ride with her in the car. The dog was happy. He liked the queen. He liked the car. He liked the treat. He barked and licked her face.

"Don't worry, Anna, I will get rid of it," her mom said, and grabbed a shoe. She tried to hit the spider, but it was too fast. It ran across the wall, and then jumped on the floor. Anna and her mom jumped back, and the spider crawled under the sofa.

"Where did it go?" Anna asked, holding her doll tight.

"It's under the sofa, but we can't reach it," her mom said, looking under the sofa. "We need something to get it out."

Anna had an idea. She remembered that her dad had a big flashlight in his room. She ran to his room, and found the flashlight on his desk. She also saw a big picture on the wall, that showed the inside of his arm. It had white and black shapes, and looked like bones.

"What is that?" Anna asked, pointing at the picture.

"That's an x-ray," her mom said, following her. "It shows what's inside your body. Your dad had to get one when he hurt his arm last month. But he's healthy now, don't worry."

Anna nodded, and took the flashlight. She ran back to the living room, and shone the flashlight under the sofa. She saw the spider, and it saw her. It crawled out from under the sofa, and ran towards the door.

"Look, mom, there it is!" Anna shouted, and followed the spider. Her mom grabbed the shoe again, and threw it at the spider. She missed, and the spider escaped through the door.

"Phew, we did it!" Anna said, and hugged her mom. "We scared the spider away!"

"Yes, we did, honey," her mom said, and hugged her back. "You were very brave, and very smart. You used the flashlight to find the spider. That was a good idea."

Anna smiled, and felt proud. She liked to help her mom, and she liked to learn new things. She wondered what else she could see with an x-ray. Lily was a little girl who loved to learn new things. She liked to read books, play with puzzles and do experiments. She had a small lab in her room, where she had a microscope, a magnifying glass and some test tubes. She wanted to be a scientist when she grew up.

One day, she found a book in the library that had pictures of animals and plants. She was very curious about them, so she borrowed the book and took it home. She looked at the book and saw a picture of a butterfly. It was very pretty, with many colors and patterns on its wings. She wanted to see a real butterfly, so she decided to go to the park.

She took her lab with her, in a backpack. She walked to the park and looked for butterflies. She saw many flowers, birds and bugs, but no butterflies. She was sad and frustrated. She thought maybe the butterflies were hiding from her.

She saw a big bush with purple flowers. She thought maybe there were butterflies inside. She went closer and peeked into the bush. She saw a small, green and yellow creature. It had a long body, six legs and two antennae. It was a caterpillar.

Lily was excited. She remembered from the book that caterpillars turn into butterflies. She wanted to see how that happened. She took out a glass jar from her lab and put the caterpillar inside. She closed the lid and smiled. She thought she had found the perfect thing for her experiment.

She took the jar and went back home. She put the jar on her desk and watched the caterpillar. She hoped it would change soon. She did not know that caterpillars need leaves and air to live. She did not know that they need time and space to make a cocoon and transform. She did not know that she was hurting the caterpillar.

The next day, she looked at the jar and saw that the caterpillar was not moving. It was still and quiet. It was dead. Lily was shocked and sad. She realized that she had made a mistake. She had taken the caterpillar away from its home and friends. She had not given it what it needed to grow and change. She had not respected its life.

She felt sorry and guilty. She wished she could bring the caterpillar back to life. She wished she could see it become a butterfly. She wished she had not been so selfish and greedy. She learned a lesson. She learned that sometimes, the best way to gain knowledge is to observe and appreciate, not to capture and control. She learned that nothing is perfect, and that everything has a value. She learned to be kind and careful with nature.

She called Tom's mom and told her what happened. Tom's mom was very angry and said, "That was very bad of Tom. He should not steal your doll. He should say sorry and give it back."

She went to Tom's room and found the sack under his bed. She opened it and saw the doll. She was shocked and said, "Tom, what did you do? This is not your doll. This is Lily's doll. You took it from her. That was very wrong."

Tom felt scared and ashamed. He knew he did a bad thing. He said, "I'm sorry, mom. I liked the doll and I wanted to have it. I did not think about Lily's feelings."

His mom said, "That is no excuse, Tom. You hurt Lily and you broke her trust. You have to return the doll and apologize to her. And you have to learn to respect other people's things and feelings."

She took the doll and the sack and went with Tom to Lily's house. She made Tom give the doll back to Lily and say he was sorry. Lily was happy to have her doll back, but she was still hurt and angry. She did not want to play with Tom anymore. She said, "Thank you for giving me my doll back, Tom. But you are not my friend anymore. You are mean and selfish. You have to earn my trust again."

Tom felt very sad and sorry. He realized he lost a friend because of his greed. He learned a hard lesson that day. He learned that stealing is wrong and that friendship is precious. He learned that he should be happy with what he has and not take what belongs to others. He learned that he should be nice and share and be kind. He learned that he should say sorry when he makes a mistake and try to make up for it. He learned that he should treat others the way he wants to be treated. He learned that he should be a good friend.

The bunny opened its mouth and said, "My name is Truth. I am a magic bunny. I can talk and grant wishes. But you have to be honest with me, or I will hop away."

Lily and Ben were amazed. They had never met a magic bunny before. They wanted to make a wish.

"Can you make us fly, Truth?" Lily asked.

"Can you make us invisible, Truth?" Ben asked.

Truth shook its head. "No, I can't do that. Those are too hard for me. I can only do simple things, like make a flower grow, or change the color of something. And you have to share one wish, not two."

Lily and Ben thought for a moment. They decided to share one wish. They whispered to each other, then told Truth their wish.

Truth smiled. "That is a good wish. And a kind one. I will grant it for you." He hopped to a nearby bench and tapped it with his paw. The bench turned into a big cake, with chocolate and strawberries, and candles on top. It smelled delicious.

Lily and Ben clapped their hands and cheered. They ran to the cake and blew out the candles. They cut a slice for themselves and one for Truth. They ate the cake and enjoyed it very much. They thanked Truth for their wish.

Truth was happy. He liked Lily and Ben. They were honest and friendly. He decided to stay with them and be their friend. They played in the park until it was dark, then they went home together. They hugged Truth and said goodbye. They promised to see him again tomorrow.

"Mom, what is that?" Philip asked excitedly.

His mom looked out over the lake and replied, "It looks like a boat, Philip, and it's coming right toward you!"

Philip watched eagerly as the boat slowly came closer. But as it came closer, he noticed that it was going backward! The boat was reversing at full speed. It seemed to be heading straight towards him.

Philip felt a chill in his bones. He was scared, but he was also curious. What could be causing such a strange wake in the lake?

When the boat was close enough, Philip finally saw what wasn't causing the wake. Inside the boat was a huge black goose, honking in excitement. The goose had its wings outspread, pushing the boat backward across the lake.

Philip laughed in delight. It had been an incredible sight to witness. In fact, it was one that he'd never forget.
